title: 8bit Dungeon Boss
description: A sort of square swing piece using very simple synths (but highly post-processed). It just makes you want to explore that dungeon, doesn't it!? 8bit Dungeon Level is similar but slower.
credit: "8bit Dungeon Boss" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: A Mission
description: Highly orchestrated pulsing piece. High energy. Driven by strings and some low brass.
credit: "A Mission" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: A Singular Perversion
description: Overplayed piano, subtle percussion, sweepy violins.
credit: "A Singular Perversion" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: A Very Brady Special
description: The Brady in the title is not a reference to the Brady Bunch. It is a reference to Dr. Brady Haran, one of the most influential filmmakers of all time.
credit: "A Very Brady Special" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Accralate
description: African-inspired lazy drum ensemble. Feel change in the middle; Tempo change near the end. Lots of polyrhythms. This piece exhibits some phantom notes athat you hear, but don't really exist. Hard to explain. Batu, Conga, Marimba, Agogo, Cowbell, Clave.
credit: "Accralate" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Aces High
description: Like a night out on the Vegas strip, Aces High makes your hips swagger with a playful bass line and staccato electric guitar. An organ plays the main theme, but when the song changes to a minor key, a clavichord plucks out the central melody, before returning to the slippery organ refrain.
credit: "Aces High" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Achaidh Cheide
description: Traditional Irish-sounding. I had a hard time classifying this in my existing feels. It feels like Irish folk music.
credit: "Achaidh Cheide" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Achilles
description: Written as theme music for an epic drama. This starts broad and kicks into awesome at 0:27.
credit: "Achilles" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Acid Trumpet
description: Cool EP, muted trumpet, and a layed back bass.
credit: "Acid Trumpet" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Action
description: Underscore for a very dramatic scene with lots of cut-outs for dialog. Tubular bells, snare, tymp, etc are all at the fore. Might be difficult to use generically, but it is quite a good cue.
credit: "Action" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Adding the Sun
description: Energizing and uplifting!
credit: "Adding the Sun" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Adeste Fideles (Shorter)
description: We start with a repeating music box theme. The cello recontextualizes the simple music boxes providing a surprising and comforting bed for the low trumpet to sing over. [/musicologist ramblings] HELLO, HOLIDAY DANCE RECITALS!  There is a shorter version of this available... because holiday dance recitals.
credit: "Adeste Fideles (Shorter)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Adventure Meme
description: It came from the GameBoy! Classic adventure style video game music in awesome style! Grab your sword! An Adventure Meme awaits!
credit: "Adventure Meme" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Adventures in Adventureland
description: You have taken charge of your destiny.  You have trained for this.  You have power and purpose. You have arrived at the Elite Five Challenge!! #symphonic #cartoony #adventure #comfyshorts
credit: "Adventures in Adventureland" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Aerosol of my Love
description: The title of this piece of music is a pun. The word "Aerosol" is a reference to a common hair product delivery method of the 1980s. "Aerosol" can very easily sound like the words "Here is all" or even "There is all".  One can effectively hear the title spoken out loud as "Here is all of my Love". But they would be wrong.   I don't like the usage of aerosols in applications where there are other delivery methods available. #ClawBangs
credit: "Aerosol of my Love" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Aftermath
description: This is a dark, almost inky feel - subtle, and texturally rich.
credit: "Aftermath" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Aggressor
description: The whole Orchestral Speed Metal genre has been done to death. But you can't consider yourself a real composer if you haven't checked "Orchestral Speed Metal" off your list. Other essential genres include: Electro Emo-Pop, Motet, Disco Noise, Adult Contemporary, Tone Poem, Haircore, and Zydeco Revival.
credit: "Aggressor" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Agnus Dei X
description: Just a quick piece from a traditional Latin mass. Lyrics are "Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi, miserere nobis._. Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi, dona nobis pacem". For Sopranos and Bass.
credit: "Agnus Dei X" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: AhDah
description: A tight slightly funky EP and drum machine driven piece featuring female voice.
credit: "AhDah" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Air Prelude
description: Slow; lots of flutes; some digital synth for texture.
credit: "Air Prelude" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Airport Lounge
description: Light and airy, this piece is guaranteed not to steal focus.
credit: "Airport Lounge" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Airship Serenity
description: This is the first slow 8-bit piece I ever tried. There was some skepticism going in, but holy man! This turned out great! You can use it for your game credits, or more chill parts of your game. Maybe at the Healing Shack, or the Abe Vigoda Memorial Pagoda and Koi Pond. The uncompressed download has a bonus  percussion track.
credit: "Airship Serenity" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Aitech
description: Hard rock beat with electronic elements grooving in.
credit: "Aitech" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Alchemists Tower
description: A crazy ride, starting calm and erupting into a frenzy. Calm again at the end. Very Elfman-like.
credit: "Alchemists Tower" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Alien Restaurant
description: Non-real instrumentation written as background music for a restaurant on another planet. Tribal, primitive, evolved. 4-tone scale.
credit: "Alien Restaurant" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: All This
description: Slow-building piece in 7-4 time.
credit: "All This" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Allada
description: Loose feeling West African rhythm with continuously phasing marimbas, and a short djembe solo in the middle.
credit: "Allada" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Almost Bliss
description: I love sipping lemonade by the lake when a storm approaches. I love walking through apple orchards in the fall.  I love the squeak of minivan tires being dragged onto the flatbed truck of the repo man. Memories of simpler times... so wonderful.
credit: "Almost Bliss" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Almost in F
description: Very long, very slow, trance-inducing piece... 36 cents sharp of the key of F. Yes, there is a good reason for that. No, I'm not going to explain it.
credit: "Almost in F" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Almost New
description: Remember when you went on summer holiday to your Auntie's house outside Nether Wallop in Hampshire while your parents went to Cyprus to broker a secret deal with the Ottoman Empire?  Remember the times in the Magic Garden? This piece of music is more "Magic Garden" than "Inter-Empire Diplomacy".
credit: "Almost New" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Amazing Grace 2011
description: Tasteful version of the classic religious piece.
credit: "Amazing Grace 2011" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Amazing Plan
description: With elements of a quick Russian polka playing in the immigrant section of industrial-era New York City, this piece is mainly in a minor key, but at the halfway point changes to a major key, reversing the feel and tone for a few seconds, before reverting to the darkness of the minor key.
credit: "Amazing Plan" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Ambiment" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ambler
description: Mid-90s styled happy happy video game music.
credit: "Ambler" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ambush

credit: "Ambush" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Americana

credit: "Anachronist" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Anamalie" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ancient Mystery Waltz (Allegro)

credit: "Ancient Rite" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ancient Winds
description: So, you want to relax, huh buddy? Do ya? You want to RELAX? Me too. Here's some beautiful sounds to listen to.
credit: "Ancient Winds" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

description: Sweet sounding French horns opposite clarinet with harps.
credit: "And Awaken" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Andreas Theme
description: This is my favorite piece that perfectly captures a slightly grown-up sound, but still sounds like a 1990s-era action-drama.  Old Way: Synthesized Electric Piano New Way: Actual EP Recordings that are built into virtual instruments that are then put through a lot of processors to make them SOUND like Synthesized Electric Pianos. Old Way: Synthesized Ocarina New Way: Assemble recordings of an ocarina player, and then make a virtual instrument that captures beautiful expression and legato lines... turn off all that fancy stuff and play it like a crappy synth.
credit: "Andreas Theme" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Android Sock Hop
description: This has a couple funny-sounding synths and plenty of whitespace. As a note to YouTube "producers"; 10 hours of this piece would be pretty mean. 1 hour of this piece isn't much better. For the sake of mankind, please do not make extended mixes of this piece. I can not be held responsible for mental anguish caused by repeated listening.
credit: "Android Sock Hop" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Angel Share
description: Starts slow and builds to an ecstasy the likes of which are almost guaranteed to garner donations from your flock! Bonus track comes with a everything except the drums in case you need a smoother feel.
credit: "Angel Share" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Angels We Have Heard on High" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Anguish" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Apprehension" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Aquarium
description: Saint-Saens' masterpiece. This piece is 100% free to use. It will probably get claimed by any number of music publishers, just so you know. They can't tell the difference between this and their copyrighted recordings. Contest the claims. Contest all the claims. I do not claim music.
credit: "Aquarium" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Arcadia
description: Many choirs in a slow-moving ethereal progression.
credit: "Arcadia" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Arcane
description: Nicely motive tribal/modern percussive fusion.
credit: "Arcane" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Aretes
description: Solo piano surrounded by rich textures.
credit: "Aretes" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Arid Foothills
description: Slight polyrhythms grow in the piece as it gains intensity. It eases back down at 2:30.
credit: "Arid Foothills" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Arroz Con Pollo
description: When I think of Cuba, I think of one thing; Nickel mines! Moa, Cuba (aka "The Sudbury of the Caribbean") has had Canadian assistance in its mining for quite some time now. From what I can tell, it is much better for Canadian companies to poison far-away water than Canadian water. Makes sense!
credit: "Arroz Con Pollo" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Artifact
description: Interesting multi-layered blend of percussion rhythms and acoustic guitar, which foreshadows the choir.
credit: "Artifact" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: As I Figure
description: Sort of Spanish, sort of Tom Waits. This one is hard to classify.
credit: "As I Figure" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ascending the Vale
description: We've all been there... wandering through an impenetrable forest, half dead with 2 arrows sticking out of your leg. And yet we continue - because it is probably good for the narrative. Then hope! Oh thank the old gods and the new!! An unmapped settlement of woodland inhabitants takes you in and brings you back from the brink of certain death. You don't even care that it is a scurry of giant squirrels that came to the rescue, or that the healing soup they give you is largely acorn-based, and vomit-inducing. Pastoral and beautiful. The download comes with a loop for if you never want the feeling to end.
credit: "Ascending the Vale" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ashton Manor
description: Flute and clarinet float over a moving and smooth string section.  Change in tone at 26 seconds in.
credit: "Ashton Manor" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Asian Drums
description: A semi-chaotic mix of drums with nice reverb.
credit: "Asian Drums" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: At Launch
description: An epic orchestral work featuring heavy brass and strings.  This piece takes the listener on a spirited journey through military might and hopeful adventure.
credit: "At Launch" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: At Rest
description: A recurring voice melody cascades over piano chords that sway in the breeze. Strings and horns then play the melody as the piano is slightly more forceful before settling again. It is suggestive of sadness, but with a sense of closure and peace.
credit: "At Rest" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: At The Shore
description: A mixture of African vocal chants and Caribbean-styled percussion and bass guitar makes you long for your hammock. The piece is relaxing and gets you in the mood for ?Island Time? - where the troubles of the world melt away in the ocean breeze.
credit: "At The Shore" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Atlantean Twilight
description: Time ticks away in a far away place in this little new-age piece.
credit: "Atlantean Twilight" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Atonal in C-ish
description: Atonal, sure... but almost in the key of C... or C-sharp. No traditional harmonics, fast paced - but measured. The fourth of a series.
credit: "Atonal in C-ish" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Attack of the Mole Men
description: Written as an introduction to a play, this has the feel of a 1950's monster movie.
credit: "Attack of the Mole Men" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Aunt Tagonist
description: Tuba and trumpets with a sting at the end. 2 short versions included, one with trumpets and one without.
credit: "Aunt Tagonist" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Aurea Carmina
description: Mid-tempo groovy hustle. Perfect for the roller-rink.
credit: "Aurea Carmina" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Autumn Day
description: A reflective piece with piano, guitar, simplified percussion, and subtle strings, this music is calm and comforting, like a good book and a hot cup of tea. The chord progressions are interesting and repeat often, which gives the piece a memorable quality.
credit: "Autumn Day" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Avant Jazz
description: Filtered vibe and horns play against a relentless bass and percussion section.
credit: "Avant Jazz" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ave Marimba
description: This music is sort of ethnic-nonethnic. It is the sort of thing you can use for your travel video to Cairo, but would also work for your travel video to Columbus, Ohio. Columbus, Ohio - Where blank canvasses become full lives! Visit Columbus on your next getaway! Coffee shops, restaurants, and many seasonal festivals provide a rich backdrop to help make your life seem slightly less desperate. Columbus, Ohio: We have a river!
credit: "Ave Marimba" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Basic Implosion

It started with me not-rapping in my childhood in the upper midwest. My lack-of-rapping hit a new high while on a high school band trip to Disneyworld, and was again bolstered in a crazy non-rap filled Spring Break in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario. There's just something about not-rapping and industrial forestry...
credit: "Basic Implosion" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Beauty Flow

Before arpeggiators, we had to find patterns in our music by using corkboards, newspaper clippings, pushpins, coloured yarn, and 8x10 black and white glossy photos.  The percussion does change during this piece, but it won't get in the way of your energetic interview.

title: Bittersweet
description: Ok, I might be crying a little bit. But it is understandable... I went to a party store, and I saw all the colorful balloons with happy sayings on them like "Get Well" and "Feel Better" and "A Hug for You"... I just started thinking how the helium will all be gone one day. Just gone... we won't get it back, and it took millions of years of radioactive decay to get the helium we have now... and... *sniff* we just don't have millions more years to wait for more. They're wasting helium in balloons... how can I possibly "Feel Better"!?
credit: "Bittersweet" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Blue Ska
description: Run of the mill ska!? No such thing! Well, this is as close to that reality as you can get. It is high energy, dance-inducing, happy fun times for everyone who was born after... like... the Industrial Revolution... So, there may be some trees and fungi that don't find this fun; but, I can't really care about their concepts of fun too much. I assume they don't like winters, but they just all sort of stand around all the time.
credit: "Blue Ska" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: BossaBossa

credit: "BossaBossa" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Brain Dance
description:
Immerse yourself in the pulsating beats of "Brain Dance," a sonic experience that plunges you deep into the heart of the Sixth World. Conjured amidst the neon glow and astral currents of a dystopian Seattle, this track is the essence of a Decker's paradise.

Synthwave textures weave an intricate matrix around you, leaving you entangled in its cybernetic allure. Deck in, chummer, and let the futuristic soundscape rewrite your reality. Wait... what universe is this set in?
credit: "Brain Dance" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 4 in G, Movement I (Allegro), BWV 1049

The primary violin is obviously sampled in a few of the faster passages, but the sweet tone shines through nicely on the slower notes. This is my first attempt at a Brandenburg... I suspect I'll revisit this one after I get a few more recorded. Still, it is probably the best free and digital recording available.
credit: "Brandenburg Concerto No. 4 in G, Movement I (Allegro), BWV 1049" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Canon in D for Autoharp
description: The autoharp is that instrument that has a pile of parallel strings that you strum while pushing buttons to make different chords. I remember these from 5th-grade music class along with flute-o-phones and recorders. What I didn't know back then, is that you can pick individual strings too! You don't have to just strum! This piece is 100% picking. A manual autoharp. Hey Mrs. Withersby, stick that in your flute-o-phone and pluck it!
credit: "Canon in D for Autoharp" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Canon in D for Two Harps
description: Harpists, by nature, are solitary people who love horses. Getting harpists to play fast together and contour a melodic line is neigh-on impossible. So we have to give all the notes to one person so it doesn't sound like harp hell. But now you need to rest, because plucking like that is insane, so the other person gets the next tough part.  You also need to make sure that each part makes sense so you can practice it and not feel like you're throwing your soul down a well.  I believe this is the best arrangement of this piece for 2 harps; A thing which should never have been tried. The arrangement itself is in the Public Domain, and sheet music is available.
credit: "Canon in D for Two Harps" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

Upbeat EDM track with a fast tempo and modern vibe. It is joyful, optimistic, and playful. Good for dynamic, high-energy sequences. A straightforward, mood-lifting piece that adds excitement and movement.


Synthwave textures weave an intricate matrix around you, leaving you entangled in its cybernetic allure. Deck in, chummer, and let the futuristic soundscape rewrite your reality. Wait... what universe is this set in?

The coyote-lizards of your night terrors do not roam here, and you can clearly read the expiration dates on all your packages. Even the hand soap. Why does the hand soap have an expiration date? title: Corruption
description: Formerly titled "Tyranid Battle Loop", this piece was written for down and dirty... and very very long battle scenes for space bug critters. But you can use it for anything you like! Got a video where you stuck a cucumber on a drone to terrorize your cat? Boom! Corruption. Or those really gross films of people removing cysts? ug. don't use this for that. Actually, why are you posting that? Don't do it. Just... ug. can't unsee...
credit: "Corruption" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Cortosis
description: Fight sequence in a galaxy far, far away. Several changes of feel throughout.
credit: "Cortosis" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Cottages
description: You know the old phrase "as relaxing as a toaster"? They meant any electrical machine, really. I think if a toaster were to make relaxing music this is it.
credit: "Cottages" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Court of the Queen
description: Slow Waltz. English Waltz. Foxtrot. Slow Fox. Regal in its construction, this waltz is meant for the ballroom floor of a grand soiree. The pizzicato strings provide the rhythm in the first half, while strings and horns play the melody. A harp accompanies a celeste in creating transitions between segments of the music. As the music crescendos into the third minute, the frivolity turns more serious, and the piece ends with a few interchangeable chords between the celeste and the horns.
credit: "Court of the Queen" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Covert Affair
description: The scene is set for a surreptitious heist or furtive affair. The fingered acoustic bass sounds woody and dark while playing against the light cymbals and the vibrant electric piano and trumpet. The individual instruments have a slight battle for dominance, but the persistence of the slick styled bass ultimately wins.
credit: "Covert Affair" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Cowboy Sting
description: Very western-sounding sting. This comes in 75, 83, and  88 beats per minute - along with a very short cut.
credit: "Cowboy Sting" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Creeping to Ship
description: Low brass / bassoons with pizz. Mild stings on the end. (written for Darker Projects' Falcon Banner Episode 4)
credit: "Creeping to Ship" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Cretaceous Dawn
description: This piece is one of three pieces that was inspired by a trip to a dinosaur-themed roadside attraction that had "dinosaur music". That music was recorded in the early 1990s, and sounds a bit cheesy today, so I tried to update it. This piece is a hybrid of triggered samples and live recordings.
credit: "Cretaceous Dawn" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Crinoline Dreams
description: You ever get the feeling to just hang out on a skating pond with a beagle?  Make sure you hit play on this track!
credit: "Crinoline Dreams" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Crisis
description: A very serious and straight dark orchestral piece. Tubular bells, bass trombone, and bass drum add a lot of low-end.
credit: "Crisis" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Crossing the Chasm
description: Adventure, Ho! Last time on "Adventure, Ho!", the mage-orc Gnarlnosh was granted 1d4 wishes from a Deck of Many Things and it totally screwed up the game balance. Why? Because the DM sort of sucks, but he thought "Oh, sure - this could be fun... how could giving a mage-orc a fully provisioned army in the middle of a desert possibly sidetrack the quest for finding a cure for a magical disease that is ruining the kingdom AND the healer elf." Deck of Many Things; BAH! More like Deck of This-Campaign-Jumped-the-Shark.
credit: "Crossing the Chasm" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Crossing the Divide
description: Americana western-sounding piece. It kicks in around 1:14. This was composed for the film "Duel" (2014).
credit: "Crossing the Divide" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Crowd Hammer
description: Originally written as an establishing shot for a psychological thriller. This has a very earthy/folky feel about it. Little slow, little edgy... I don't know. Take a listen. I mean, I'll keep trying to describe this but, I'm not doing too well here. There's this flute thing... uhh... Slightly creepy movie score? Yet oddly comforting? Sure. Let's go with that.
credit: "Crowd Hammer" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Cruising for Goblins
description: Dear Green Valkyrie, Your life force is running out. Green Valkyrie needs food badly. Remember; Don't shoot food. Someone shot the food. Your shots now hurt other players. You just shot the potion. C'mon Green Valkyrie, you got no chill.
credit: "Cruising for Goblins" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Crunk Knight
description: Medieval meets club beats.
credit: "Crunk Knight" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Crusade
description: Written as travelling music for a video game... this is probably a bit too active for that. There is a beautiful choral section in the trombones at 2:18. Good anvils.
credit: "Crusade" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Crusade - Heavy Industry
description: Do you have recurring dreams of being an industrial roomba working in an ore processing facility? Do you make fantasy paintings and need some music for timelapses? Do you go jog-hopping in low-gravity post-apocalyptic environments? Do you have opinions about eggs? Are you a monster who is in charge of other monsters? Did you work on a top-hat/sombrero assembly line? Are you starting a ferry line on the river Acheron to compete with Charon? Are you drafting epic legislation? Do you enjoy hitting dumpsters with sticks?
credit: "Crusade - Heavy Industry" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Cryptic Sorrow
description: Sad solo piano with a "reality" feel. Uneven meters.
credit: "Cryptic Sorrow" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Crypto
description: Very moody little piece with some melodic interest. Tension could be high grade or low grade depending on your context. Waiting for a drug deal to go through in Belize? This'll work. Concerned about the health of your hyacinth macaw while waiting at the vet office? This'll work. Waiting for the OSHA all-clear at your box factory? This'll work. It is mainly about waiting for things. Probably not good things.
credit: "Crypto" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Cuban Sandwich
description: A groovy little piece excellent for an evening at your local cabana.
credit: "Cuban Sandwich" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Cupid's Revenge
description: Celestial themed video game music.
credit: "Cupid's Revenge" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Curse of the Scarab
description: Five! Five full minutes of battle fighting action bits with a bit of an Egyptian flair! For some reason I associate English horn with desert nomads. There must have been some cultural reference in my youth to that effect. Super crazy awesome brass is super crazy awesome... wait for it... you'll be glad you did! Uncompressed download comes with fully loopable mix.
credit: "Curse of the Scarab" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Cut and Dry
description: Modern-style production of a dance/world music fusion. Laser sharp super compressed mix.
credit: "Cut and Dry" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Cut and Run
description: Modern club music.
credit: "Cut and Run" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Cut Trance
description: Semi-trance, semi-techno with a couple of touches of piano. Pretty driving for being so slow. Super super clean mix that'll rattle your walls.
credit: "Cut Trance" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Cyborg Ninja
description: Your girlfriend has be kidnapped by ninja! Stage 1: Desert. Avoid the flaming balls and shoot cyborg ninja in the eye to win round. Retro-gaming circa 1988. I was seriously considering naming this piece "Flaming Balls" as that would also have been appropriate. Cyborg ninjas are just a little more '1988' to me. Need 10 hours of this? Loop it!
credit: "Cyborg Ninja" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Daily Beetle
description: We have ways of making you happy! This is one of them. Super catchy mid-tempo grooving ukulele-driven happy music. Useful for: feel-good stories, sentimental retrospectives, Minecraft montages, shark attacks, coming of age stories, cooking shows, and baby raves.
credit: "Daily Beetle" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dama-May
description: Simple oddly asynchronous piece where the percussion and melody get along, but in an aloof sort of way.
credit: "Dama-May" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dance Monster
description: A remix of one of my own pieces "120 BPM Monster" by special request. This one is longer, and more sharply mixed.
credit: "Dance Monster" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dance of Deception
description: Pipe organ piece. This is apparently a 'Czardas', a traditional Hungarian folk dance. I would like to thank Keith for the info.
credit: "Dance of Deception" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairies
description: Tchaikovsky's famous dance from the Nutcracker Suite.
credit: "Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairies" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy
description: Tchaikovsky's piece, amped up a little bit and slightly arranged for more punch and bass.
credit: "Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dance of the Tuba Plum Fairy
description: Mrs. Johnson's 4 grade band presents Tchaikovsky's "Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairies"! Featuring: Jacob on Tuba, Hailey on Euphonium, Kaylee and Caleb on Trombone, Jayden and Joey on Trumpet, Riley on Bass Drum, Abigail on Snare Drum, Zoey on Cymbals, Aubrey on Glockenspiel, Ethan on Sleigh Bells, and Mrs. Johnson on Piano. Arrangement by Kevin MacLeod.
credit: "Dance of the Tuba Plum Fairy" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dances and Dames
description: Off-center feeling film noir-like piece with a continually changing time signature. "Something is amiss on the streets. My job is to figure that out."
credit: "Dances and Dames" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Danger Storm
description: So this one sounds like what is sounds like. The high quality download has a few bonus mixes. The Tin Mix is excellent for small speakers. The Phased Mix is like... sort of groovy, man. The 90 mix is a bit faster. And the House Mix is super dance party fun times!
credit: "Danger Storm" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dangerous
description: Crescendo and sting at the end.
credit: "Dangerous" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Danse Macabre
description: Written by Saint Saens in 1874. This is a quite well known and epic piece of music.
credit: "Danse Macabre" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Danse Macabre - Big Hit 1
description: A 2 note hit from a section change in Danse Macabre. It can be used as a very short ending sting.
credit: "Danse Macabre - Big Hit 1" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Danse Macabre - Big Hit 2
description: Another 2-note hit from the interior of Danse Macabre.
credit: "Danse Macabre - Big Hit 2" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Danse Macabre - Busy Strings
description: An interesting section of Danse Macabre from around measure 145. There is a particularly nice viola trill with ornament.
credit: "Danse Macabre - Busy Strings" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Danse Macabre - Finale
description: Just the finale from the "Danse Macabre". This is the highest energy portion of the piece in isolation.
credit: "Danse Macabre - Finale" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Danse Macabre - Light Dance
description: A small section of Danse Macabre that features the basses, cellos, and violas each taking one beat out of the measure with a triplet. Light melody on the top.
credit: "Danse Macabre - Light Dance" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Danse Macabre - Low Strings Finale
description: Just the low strings and brass from the finale of "Danse Macabre".
credit: "Danse Macabre - Low Strings Finale" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Danse Morialta
description: Simple, simple, effective piano piece. This one is hard to pin down emotionally, so I marked it at both somber and uplifting. It is really quite good... though not quite Satie.
credit: "Danse Morialta" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Danse of Questionable Tuning
description: Interesting piano and cello piece.  As title suggests, there is some questionable tuning.  Piece begins with piano, brings in cello around 00:05, both continue until the end of the piece.
credit: "Danse of Questionable Tuning" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dark Dance
description: Winds, piano, and brass come in very late. The piece accelerates to the end.
credit: "Dark Dance" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dark Fog
description: The title refers to a state of mind more than a physical thing. That sort of feeling you get when there are choices to be made... none of them very good ones.
credit: "Dark Fog" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dark Hallway (clean)
description: Clean version of this piece. 2 sections; one choppy, and one smooth. (see also distressed)
credit: "Dark Hallway (clean)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dark Hallway (distressed)
description: Distressed (1930's era vinyl) version of this piece. 2 sections; one choppy, and one smooth.
credit: "Dark Hallway (distressed)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dark Pad
description: This is a dark and eerie arrhythmic thing with deep lows and cutting highs. Experimental only in the personal sense - I just got GarageBand, and I'm seeing what the (very nice) electronic effects can do.
credit: "Dark Pad" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dark Standoff
description: Broad dark sustained chords in the low strings punctuated with slight percussion.
credit: "Dark Standoff" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dark Star
description: Dark Star is a orchestral fanfare featuring a rising motive led by the brass and strings.  The piece builds gradually and finishes with a full orchestral climax.
credit: "Dark Star" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dark Times
description: Deeply troubling and somber, this piece is heavy on the bass strings, especially in the last minute. The feel is very dark and funereal, and could be used to depict the beginning of the apocalypse.
credit: "Dark Times" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dark Walk
description: Simple motive countered by several striking dissonances.
credit: "Dark Walk" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Darkening Developments
description: Bass is very VERY strong in this. Please make sure you master on a system capable of reproducing these notes. The end feel is decided different from the rest of the piece. It does an unnerving build to nowhere.
credit: "Darkening Developments" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Darkest Child
description: A childlike celeste plays high notes among a barely audible harp and deep bass. In the second minute the disturbing melody is in a lower register, and strings accentuate the discordant sounds before returning to the high register. The music is excellent for a creepy dream sequence or the exposition of an unknown fantasy world. SMARTSOUND
credit: "Darkest Child" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Darkest Child var A
description: A notably quicker version of "Darkest Child".
credit: "Darkest Child var A" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Darkling
description: Pulsing Dooom! Recommended for use in all your various adventure-y side-scrollers with lots of shooting or stabbing, and the occasional jump-scare. Should loop really great!
credit: "Darkling" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Darkness is Coming
description: Quiet yet epic. This piece is an odd mix. Highly processed drum kit.
credit: "Darkness is Coming" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Darkness Speaks
credit: "Darkness Speaks" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: DarxieLand
description: A rousingly comedic romp on the dark side of Dixieland music, featuring a wonderfully questionable trumpet player!
credit: "DarxieLand" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Day of Chaos
description: Abrasive upright piano sets the tone for this start-stop horror suspense piece.
credit: "Day of Chaos" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Daybreak
description: Solo vintage electric piano. Lounge/New Age.
credit: "Daybreak" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Daytime TV Theme
description: Slow and deliberate.
credit: "Daytime TV Theme" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: DD Groove
description: Very laid-back piece that may be indicative of a loss, or possibly carelessness.
credit: "DD Groove" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dead Drop
description: Super nice drum fills and guitar work. Deliberate pace... like someone is on a mission.
credit: "Dead Drop" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Deadly Roulette
description: Jazzy! Gumshoe-y! Mystery-y! I suck at making adjectives. Who needs adjectives anyway! I'm fine without adjectives. How fine without adjectives, you may ask? I can't say - as that would require some sort of descriptor! And I don't need descriptors in my writings... Maybe one... tiny little... NO! What am I thinking!? I refuse! I've completely had it with adjectives! Hah! Adverbs work perfectly fine! Woohoo! Adverbs! And before I get mail... adjectives killed my family, so I can go off on them all I want.
credit: "Deadly Roulette" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Death and Axes
description: Holy epic action. Just look at the instruments in this! The piece shall now speak for itself.
credit: "Death and Axes" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Death of Kings
description: Deep and rich piece of remembrance for brass. The melody is carried by the horn, with some help later by trumpets.
credit: "Death of Kings" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Decay
description: A very dark piece heavily featuring cymbal and bells.  Frequent Cymbal usage creates unnerving feeling.  3:08 prolonged trombone.  Lasts almost 30 seconds.  This piece is great for an eerie atmosphere.
credit: "Decay" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Decisions
description: A vocal chorus blends with subtle percussion and panning synth effects that rattles the bones. The choir rises in volume almost imperceptibly before dissolving, leaving a sense of drama and consequence. Perfect for the background music to build suspense and intrigue. Loopable.
credit: "Decisions" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Deck the Halls A
description: Piano solo of the traditional holiday piece. Very smooth with seemingly random phrasing. This isn't really a sing-along type recording.
credit: "Deck the Halls A" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Deck the Halls B
description: Repeating, peppy sing-along version of the holiday classic.
credit: "Deck the Halls B" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Decline
description: Slow and mildly creepy with a hint of beautiful.
credit: "Decline" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Deep and Dirty
description: I'm awake, I'm awake! Okay! Holy man! Wow. That is a lot.
credit: "Deep and Dirty" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Deep Haze
description: A lighter piece than the descriptors would imply. It is more hollow than dark, more motion-forward than driving. Builds continuously but slowly.
credit: "Deep Haze" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Deep Noise
description: Could be breathing, could be the wind, it is very dark, and kind of disturbing.
credit: "Deep Noise" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Deep Relaxation
description: The main melody is a stack of harp, piano, and electric piano. The bass is just a nice mono synth.
credit: "Deep Relaxation" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Del Rio Bravo
description: I'm gonna come clean here. I have no idea what this is. Mexican? Maybe? Dance music? Drinking music? I don't even understand what this would do culturally.
credit: "Del Rio Bravo" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Delightful D
description: Welcome to the Holiday Inn, Airport. The presentation will begin shortly.   SUCCESS starts with your ATTITUDE!   If you are not EARNING, make sure you are LEARNING!   AMBITION is the path to success. PERSISTENCE is the vehicle you arrive in.  Success is doing the OPPOSITE of what everyone else is DOING!   Actually... don't take this last one too literally. If everyone else is using the door, don't try walking through a wall (or whatever the opposite of a "door" is). I mean... there is a reason most people do the same things. Usually because they make sense. Oh, sure... it is okay to QUESTION what people are doing, but just doing the opposite... probably not great.   The future of NETWORK MARKETING is UNLIMITED!   Oh... Also a bit of hyperbole here. I mean, it literally cannot exceed the gross output of all the world's economies - and will likely top out far before that due to INEFFICIENCIES and REGULATION.

title: Destiny Day
description: My work has been seminal in the development of 'structuredly-non-linear symmetrical-music', a highly intellectual, and rather repetitive genre. My newest piece studies, experiences and isomorphically dominates a variety of structured tension-hemiolas. In short, the method must never present the sound-world. I never examine continuities, despite the fact that any gesture or non-linearity can be, and has been interpreted as a rather orchestrally-monophonic set of 'canon-aerophones'. In my most recent work, vibrations, materials and rhythmic oscillations are all used within chaotically-transdisciplinary gestures, allowing the audience to improvise a variety of symbolic idioms. I am very much influenced by the idea of dismissing popular solos, particularly whilst combined with a highly polyrhythmic approach to spaces.
credit: "Destiny Day" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Dewdrop Fantasy
description: The smell of a garden hose, that muted crack when you start up a glowstick, watching the sunrise with a glass of freshly squeezed orange juice... all so calming... This piece of music is like that. Simple, bleeping, and slowly changing. Can you think of something else that is simple, bleeping, and changing? "an old PC speaker?" well, that's simple and bleeping. "EDM?" that's... bleeping and changing. "Hippie fashion?" that's... Hippie fashion? I don't know what that is. Well, it is long hair and paisley bell-bottoms and far too many beads... You just found the outside of the Venn Diagram.

title: Disco Medusae
description: Discomedusae is an obsolesced class of jellyfish. I'm guessing there was some biology schism back in the day and some crazy jellyfish specialist wrote some sort of definitive work on the animals and everyone had to change their classification. The jerk. I mean, it was probably JUST FINE the way it was! But NOOooo! You had to come along and screw up my perfectly good taxonomy key - rendering it USELESS! Hey jellyfish specialist - guess what? No one cares that much anyway! We're all just placating you until you die, and then everyone is going back to using the old keys, which we could at least figure out! This is a disco tune.

I don't remember what I was doing, but I was apparently dealing with fear and hope and apprehension... at least that is what it sounds like to me today - months later. Every now and again, I'll find these files - they are something of an emotional journal. Hope you enjoy it as much as I do! Download has the original MIDI file!

title: Divertissement - Pizzicato (from the ballet Sylvia)
description: Delibes. I am astounded that there are so few recordings of this piece on the net... for a few reasons.    1. Everyone knows this piece (but nearly no one knows what it is called).    2. It is very easy to record (Pizzicato strings have been one of the few samples that have sounded "real" for a long time).    3. The composer is long dead and his stuff is in the Public Domain (Léo Delibes; 1891). And for some background... Sylvia is a 3-Act ballet first produced in 1876. I'm pretty certain this particular piece has nothing to do with the plot - or it wouldn't be called a "divertissement".
credit: "Divertissement - Pizzicato (from the ballet Sylvia)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

I was listening to Lo-Fi Glitch at the time, which should explain a few things. Behold! Lo-Fi Trap! Dream Catcher! Get it? A Dream Catcher is a lo-fi trap! HAHAHHAHAhahaha! I already upgraded from a Dream Catcher to a Dream Glue Trap. You can get the dreams off with corn oil. They won't be happy. Wear thick gloves.
