title: Electrodoodle
description: Yeah, it is happy. Yeah, it is simple. Yeah, there are... rhythmic things going on. How will you use this? honestly, I have no clue.
credit: "Electrodoodle" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Elf Meditation
description: What is meditation for one may be cause for concern in another. - Some Elf
credit: "Elf Meditation" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Enchanted Journey
description: A harp solo in several distinct sections. It works well as a contained piece, but also contains several smaller sections that stand alone.
credit: "Enchanted Journey" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Enchanted Valley
description: Nice light little piece.
credit: "Enchanted Valley" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: End of the Era
description: Alto Flute along with the low brass in the beginning, switching to strings. Final sounds are more harsh than the beginning. Ends with a tiny flourish.
credit: "End of the Era" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Energizing
description: Purity is the word! Start your day with energy from this piece. Recommend you set it as your alarm!
credit: "Energizing" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Enigma
description: Written as a theme for a podcast, this was requested as "upbeat with an air of mystery". So that's what it is.
credit: "Enigma" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Enter the Maze
description: A thumping bass note intermingles with metallic noises to create a feeling of tension and terror. Screeching synth noises enter occasionally, and after a shrill screaming lead, the percussion is sparse but nerve-racking.
credit: "Enter the Maze" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Enter the Party
description: Simple, clean, light-yet-driving funk-type dance.
credit: "Enter the Party" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Envision
description: There is a mystery that is unfolding, unraveling, being solved, confounding, being thought about, being copied, demanding attention, delighting, comforting, and feeding the dog treats that look like sausages and get your hands all oily. Best for: Feature films where the protagonist thinks about a hard problem while walking at night in the neon-bathed entertainment district in Osaka in the rain in 1994.
credit: "Envision" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Epic Unease
description: Starts quiet, ends fortissimo brass.
credit: "Epic Unease" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Equatorial Complex
description:
Enjoy a serene sanctuary where time stands still. Envelop yourself in a warm, nostalgic embrace, evoking the feeling of a sun-drenched afternoon in a hidden garden. The air is filled with the echoes of a distant, yet familiar, world, inviting you to lose yourself in the comforting simplicity of the moment...


Synthwave textures weave an intricate matrix around you, leaving you entangled in its cybernetic allure. Deck in, chummer, and let the futuristic soundscape rewrite your reality. Wait... what universe is this set in?
credit: "Equatorial Complex" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Errigal
description: Celtic-sounding solo piece with a sort of drone bass line, apreggios, and a forte melody.
credit: "Errigal" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Eternal Hope
description: Building hopeful piece. Supported piano solo.
credit: "Eternal Hope" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Eternal Terminal
description: I like the waterphone in this piece. It is a bunch of metal tubes welded together, and played with a bow. It is that creepy high-pitched thing you hear in horror movies all the time.
credit: "Eternal Terminal" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Eternity
description: This is like... the ultimate in high-class non-offensive music. You can have this going at the hippest highest-class hotel in the world, and it'll feel at home. You can also put in less-classy places to make them feel classier! Like the opium den you built in your garage, or that tiny closet at your office where lunch-room recyclables go to get sticky and smell bad. I mean seriously... I don't think they ALL started out sticky.
credit: "Eternity" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ether Disco
description: More subdued bassline, and some fun glockenspiel action. Some synth drum hits.
credit: "Ether Disco" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ether Vox
description: What do you get when you cross Phil Collins and Enya? You get a visit from the ethics department, and you get your funding revoked.
credit: "Ether Vox" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ethereal Relaxation
description: Meditation Tips: 1) Get comfortable. Maybe try sitting on a chair, or the ground. 2) Breathe. Why are you holding your breath? That won't help. 3) Relax. Stop fighting the bear. You two can fight later. 4) Close your eyes. Meditation is less effective if you have toothpicks holding your eyes open. 5) Minimize distractions. Turn off all your sirens and strobe lights.  Why? Why do you even have sirens!? The bear I can understand, but why SO MANY SIRENS!?
credit: "Ethereal Relaxation" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ethernight Club
description: 2am. It is raining and there is a line outside the noodle place. A dim red glow comes up from the next staircase down; you hear a hypnotic pulse. Looking down, you see there's a propped-open door with a couple smoking outside it. "Ethernight Club" is laser cut into a piece of old roofing metal.  If you walk down the stairs to "Ethernight Club"", turn to page 13. If you decide to get noodles at ????, turn to page 42.
credit: "Ethernight Club" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Evening
description: Hey Music Supervisors! Are you sick of choosing Claude Debussy's "Clair de Lune" or Ravel's "Pavane for a Dead Princess" when you're placing music for that one scene at the end of Act II where there is a sunset and an overall sense of relief? I got ya, friend!
credit: "Evening" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Evening Fall (Harp)
description: Harp "duet"... where the harps never actually play together. Impromptu
credit: "Evening Fall (Harp)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Evening Fall (Piano)
description: Impromptu
credit: "Evening Fall (Piano)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Evening Melodrama
description: Theme for a 1980's-esque prime time TV melodrama.
credit: "Evening Melodrama" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Evening of Chaos
description: Semi-beautiful and flawed piano melody contrasts with industrial percussion.
credit: "Evening of Chaos" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ever Mindful
description: A different kind of relaxing piece with long but detailed harmonic complexity. I personally have a hard time with the drone-type of relaxing music. It doesn't work for me. This one gives your mind something to think about... very very slowly.
credit: "Ever Mindful" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Evil March
description: Description pending.
credit: "Evil March" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Evil Plan
description: Melody in the bass. Dark, but still energetic.
credit: "Evil Plan" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Exciting Trailer
description: A militaristic snare drum march begins this piece, reminiscent of Eastern Europe during World War II. The orchestral sounds blend with the sharpness of the brass throughout, but especially after 0:36, when the music is lyrical and melodic, though intensely emotional and suspenseful. At 0:52, the rhythmic march begins again, with the strings playing the melody and the brass reaching discordant, swelling heights until the final crescendo at 1:10.
credit: "Exciting Trailer" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Exhilarate
description: Exuberant and precise rock piece.
credit: "Exhilarate" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Exit the Premises
description: Big drums start with piece to reveal that they were not establishing the downbeat. Tight synth percussion and 8-bit inspired synths make this piece downright danceable! And who doesn't like a giant 80s synth? Or a 90s chip tunes synth? Or a modern synth? We gots them all!
credit: "Exit the Premises" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Exotic Battle
description: Definite African influence on this mostly orchestral piece. Clean ending.
credit: "Exotic Battle" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Exotics
description: Epic piano playing against world percussion and acid-style synths with an upbeat beat.
credit: "Exotics" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Expeditionary
description: A sort of African/European salad mix of sounds.
credit: "Expeditionary" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Eyes Gone Wrong
description: How wrong? Guess you'll need to find out.
credit: "Eyes Gone Wrong" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Facile
description: Slow, deliberate piano solo - ending on a very satisfying Tierce de Picardie.
credit: "Facile" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Failing Defense
description: This piece begins immediately with horn blasts, strings, and a bone-jangling xylophone. After the brief intro the horns play a melody, then the horns drop away away except tribal drums and staccato string bursts. The music returns in a big way, suggestive of a tense battle, as the instruments compete against each other, until the rapid discordant end.
credit: "Failing Defense" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fairytale Waltz
description: Written as an overture to (of all things) a fairy tale musical - this piece stands well on its own.
credit: "Fairytale Waltz" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fanfare for Space
description: A take-off on Strauss' Zarathustra theme that is legal for use in every country. Because I wrote it, and I said so.
credit: "Fanfare for Space" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fantasia Fantasia
description: On your journey to the Southern Oracle, you will pass many wondrous things indeed! The Morning Meal Guild, The Highest Possible Weapon, and The Dancer of Flashes all await. Never give up and good luck will find you.
credit: "Fantasia Fantasia" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fantastic Dim Bar
description: I knew I'd find a use for the subtle demonic piano! Short impromptu, dim and dark.
credit: "Fantastic Dim Bar" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Farm
description: Farm is part of a 4-part video game experience.  You can experience “Farm” here: https://incompetech.com/games/Magic%20Scout/ It even works on most phones!  TIP! Crops regrow faster than weeds.  TIP! Once a rock is magicked away, it is gone forever. Stay clear if you want to keep it!
credit: "Farm" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Farting Around
description: Every generation has its masterpiece; Bach's Brandenburg Concertos, Beethoven's 9th Symphony, Rossini's "William Tell". This is such a piece. For nearly one minute, "Farting Around" will transport you to a new world. A world of unadulterated joy. A world of pure farts.
credit: "Farting Around" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fast Talkin
description: Noir. Private detective from the 1940's sort of feel.
credit: "Fast Talkin" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Faster Does It
description: Fast-paced and frenetic, the acoustic bass plays in every register available to the instrument, while the drum kit is chaotic and harried. You know... Bebop.
credit: "Faster Does It" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fearless First
description: Before you complain about the bass, that is the entire point of this mix. It is scary-bass... yet somehow subdued. If this bass was a car, it would be a cement mixer... That's a terrible analogy. Forgetting for the moment that a cement mixer isn't a car... I guess they have the ones that are mounted on big trucks - and those trucks share a lot in common with cars, you know steering wheels, engines, tires, and the soon-to-be-anachronistic internal combustion engine. Anyway, if you don't like the bass you can pretty easily EQ it to a reasonable level, or buy the stems and remix it yourownself. Before you complain about the use of the word "yourownself", I wrote it. You understood it. It is a word. There is also some dreamy flute in here.
credit: "Fearless First" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Feather Waltz
credit: "Feather Waltz" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Feelin Good
description: A super-peppy mindless strumming feel-good sort of piece.
credit: "Feelin Good" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Feral Angel Waltz
description: Featuring the genuine Nordic Metal talents of Alexander Nakarada. This is a thing the Viennese would totally dance to... if they were MUCH more angry than average Wiener. I'm looking at you, Gunther!
credit: "Feral Angel Waltz" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Feral Chase
description: Someone's running from something... or to somewhere... High energy, but reserved.
credit: "Feral Chase" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fiddles McGinty
description: Jig? Reel? Hornpipe? I don't know!
credit: "Fiddles McGinty" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fife and Drum
description: Welcome to Historic Williamsburg! Nestled between "That's-OK Greenpoint" and "Still-Kinda-Frightening-In-Many-Areas Bushwick", Historic Williamsburg offers you a link to the past that you'll love! Trucker hats, coffee shops, mustache wax, artisanal mac+cheese, used book stores - come experience part of America's Past! And when you're done; "Get the 'L out of Williamsburg!" [ *L may not be running. ]
credit: "Fife and Drum" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fig Leaf Rag
description: The classic ragtime ditty of Scott Joplin, perfect for a silent film of whimsy and humor. The piece begins with a short intro, then plays the bouncy rhythm of with a bright plodding beat. At the end of the third minute, the pace quickens, and leads into a darker refrain, but the jolly melody returns for the finale.
credit: "Fig Leaf Rag" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fig Leaf Rag - distressed
description: The classic ragtime ditty of Scott Joplin, perfect for a silent film of whimsy and humor. The piece begins with a short intro, then plays the bouncy rhythm of with a bright plodding beat. At the end of the third minute, the pace quickens, and leads into a darker refrain, but the jolly melody returns for the finale.  With added record player effects.
credit: "Fig Leaf Rag - distressed" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fig Leaf Times Two
description: My first true Baroom Piano sound. chorusing detuned on the upper strings. Very warm sound.
credit: "Fig Leaf Times Two" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Final Battle of the Dark Wizards
description: Slowly building tension power that really gets going when the super gnarly drums kick in after the violas... sort of in the section with the trumpet.... then there's this part that's all like "AHHHH AHHHHHH AAAAAHHHHHHHHH!!!!" And then there's some more "AHHHHHHHHH" and then even more and its like a new key or something, and the drums are all distorted and slammin', and then there's this wwwwwwhhhhHHHHHOOOOOOOSHHHH!!!! and some more french horn majesty - and like another keychange or something... but definitely some bass drum. The big bass drum that you stand up and hit with a mallet... not the kind you stick on the floor... and stomp on a pedal that is attached to a mallet that hits the floor drum.
credit: "Final Battle of the Dark Wizards" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Final Count
description: Epic piece taking off from Chopin's famous funeral march (Piano Sonata #2). Death! Death! Death!
credit: "Final Count" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Finding Movement
description: The koto in this piece follows a steady, plodding beat, while the orchestral strings provide a drone-like background. At 0:33 the strings crescendo to follow the melody of the koto, but at 1:18 the tempo slows and the strings fade away, only to return to highlight the final chord.  With the even rhythm and the sharply accentuated plucks of the koto, this is best used as an introduction to a short film or game, or the resolution to a conflict surrounding family or challenges to tradition.
credit: "Finding Movement" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Finding the Balance
description: The beginning is calm with the Middle Eastern dudek playing the melody. As the electronic elements melt into the dudek and the plucked strings, the groove is established.  Just into the third minute the melody changes to beautiful and touching, but returns to the feel of the intro, while a woman?s voice sings a haunting melody in a distant language. This is music of wonder, and is best as exposition music for a film about nature or a group of people struggling to survive.
credit: "Finding the Balance" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fire Prelude
description: Edgy/calm background music. Synth pads with some orchestral textures.
credit: "Fire Prelude" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Firebrand
description: Super fast percussive piece with polynesian rhythms mixed with a fusion of large modern drums.
credit: "Firebrand" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fireflies and Stardust
description: Some beautiful rural americana-type music. I mean, just listen to that!  It is an 8 piece ensemble, and everyone is playing a lot of notes, yet it remains so simple.  Okay, the violins aren't playing that many notes... had to pick up the 2nd violin off the waiver wires, and there wasn't enough time to get her up to speed on the offense for this piece. So we made an executive decision, and kept things simple. We should still be able to get some good yardage here, and hope to win on defense.
credit: "Fireflies and Stardust" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Firesong
description: Native American drumming with a deep dark drive. Slowly picks up in speed throughout.
credit: "Firesong" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Firmament
description: An interesting mix of rock, reggae with a more than average bit of swing to it. Three distinct snare drums give it character.
credit: "Firmament" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: First Call
description: AKA "Warning Call". Three trumpeter version of the 1804 military bugle call. I couldn't get the ensemble to do triple tonguing on the arpeggios. Oh well. Still does the job. Get ready!
credit: "First Call" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Five Armies
description: Big giant building piece starting in 6/4 alternating to 4/4 and back. Soaring ending with a lot of brass.
credit: "Five Armies" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Five Card Shuffle
description: Walkin' along blues shuffle. Accellerates beginning to end.
credit: "Five Card Shuffle" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Flighty Theme
description: Fun little piece played very poorly.
credit: "Flighty Theme" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Floating Cities
description: It is the future? It certainly sounds like it... What would I use this for? Probably a video game with non-action gameplay. Certainly a montage of some futuristic film... or maybe one of those sandwiched scenes where a person is walking in the rain, but you don't get any of the sounds of the actual rain... just this piece. No dialog, no voiceover, just walking. Do they have a name for those scenes? They must.
credit: "Floating Cities" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fluffing a Duck
description: A trombone plays a humorous melody alongside timpanis and a variety of woodwind instruments. This music is suited for a short theme for a comedic piece that relies on visual jokes.  2 Small versions in one file.
credit: "Fluffing a Duck" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Fluidscape
description: Very long, cool, relaxed piece - no surprises, though the timbre does change from time to time.
credit: "Fluidscape" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Flutey Funk
description: Starts off strong with bass, kit and flute.  Flute taking melody throughout the piece.  Bass and kit in the background throughout, however bass is prominent over kit.
credit: "Flutey Funk" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Flutey Sting
description: Slight slow down in tempo on the end.
credit: "Flutey Sting" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Flying Kerfuffle
description: Happy happy, happy happiness. Happier, happiest? Happy. Now that the word has lost all meaning, take a listen to this thing. It is dripping with joy. Ever see a sad person on a jetski? Of course not. It isn't possible. Similarly, you can't listen to this and be sad. No Mortal Can! You can be angry at it, you can dislike it, but you can't be sad because of it. What happens when you employ modern club music techniques on music for folk dances? This.
credit: "Flying Kerfuffle" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Folk Round
description: A simple folk perpetual canon - also known as a round. Feels like a medieval campfire piece.
credit: "Folk Round" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: For Originz
description: Heavy strings play several chords before a violin enters with a sliding melody, in tandem with a woman?s voice and flute. The bass drums are barely perceptible, but accentuate the orchestra as the three melodic personalities float amongst the music. The music is full of wonder and power, and ends in a strong chord, evoking a connection with nature.

credit: "Galway" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Garden Music

You can just put this one on and drift away to the imagined utopian land of your choosing! Suitable for day-spa background music, dental office calming music, very long form landscape or train videos, governmental intake and processing videos. The uncompressed download does not contain separate files, just the one big 650 meg wav file.

The are 3 tempos to practice different styles of waltz, or just work up to the fast one!

title: Gregorian Chant
description: Is it a real Gregorian Chant? Nope. For one - there are no real words in it. Honestly, I don't want a religious exaltation mucking up my fantasy world. So if you're building a historically accurate "Monk Simulator: Year of Our Lord 882!", just move on. The other reason this isn't real is I never learned how to read that notation. There are insufficient sticks for the rhythms in the notation... I know, there is a real convention that you can learn. I just grabbed a few pieces of the sheet music from the 1200s, and guessed at how to do it. Sounds reasonable enough to me! (says the guy who knows virtually nothing about the art)
credit: "Gregorian Chant" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

They really sound quite intentional. Why else would I write something like that? Totally done with forethought. Yup. 100% on purpose.

credit: "Groove Grove" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

Or your real estate tour... Or your appendectomy video... Or your video of that one train by your house. Uncompressed download comes with a faster version, and a slower version.
credit: "Groundwork" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Guess Who
description: Bizarre mix of orchestral setting with a power guitar and drum set.
credit: "Guess Who" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Guiton Sketch
description: Very short and energetic piece - but it can be easily looped, the end lines up perfectly with the beginning.
credit: "Guiton Sketch" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Gustav Sting
description: A grooving sting featuring percussion and low staccato strings.
credit: "Gustav Sting" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Guts and Bourbon
description: Country... rural... upbeat...
credit: "Guts and Bourbon" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Guzheng City
description: Welcome to "Hotel Lobbies Around the World"! Here in Guzheng City, this hotel lobby features flaming brasiers offset the triple 10 meter waterfalls.  An innovative clock made of animatronic dolphins sets the tone, while telling the time! 6 Artist alcoves on the opposite wall provide guests with entertainment while providing the artists customers! Next week, we will take a look at a very special taxidermy-themed lobby in Cudahy, Wisconsin.
credit: "Guzheng City" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Gymnopedie No. 1
description: Elegant and slightly dark, the simplicity of the piano melody is light and touching, with a feeling of pensive restraint. It is beautiful accompaniment to the close of a drama, or of a midday reverie. Composed by Erik Satie.
credit: "Gymnopedie No. 1" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Gymnopedie No. 2
description: This piece is dramatic and very dynamic; in the beginning and towards the end the music is soft and tender, but it is punctuated by aggressive changes in volume and minor chords throughout. This piece could work well to depict grief, as the emotions and feelings are similarly mercurial. Composed by Erik Satie.
credit: "Gymnopedie No. 2" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Gymnopedie No. 3
description: A slow waltz with a beautiful and haunting melody played mostly in the higher registers. A few notes were added to Satie?s composition to keep things interesting and give the music a more full sound, the music ends with a very dark chord. This music is sad and tragic, and could be used as accompaniment to a slow dance or an art house film. Composed by Erik Satie.
credit: "Gymnopedie No. 3" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Gypsy Shoegazer
description: No, I don't know what this is. Some sort of Bulgarian dirge? It has a good 2-part folk melody that is pretty easy to sing, and a wonderful B section with super cadences at the middle and end.
credit: "Gypsy Shoegazer" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Gypsy Shoegazer No Voices
description: No, I don't know what this is. Same as Gypsy Shoegazer, but without the vocal parts... in case you want to add you own vocal parts.
credit: "Gypsy Shoegazer No Voices" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Habanera
description: The famous Habanera aria from Georges Bizet's opera "Carmen". Sung by Jenny Lee Mitchell.
credit: "Habanera" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hackbeat
description: Only obliquely Latin, I didn't know how else to classify this one. No melody.
credit: "Hackbeat" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Half Mystery
description: They make you think, but not too much. When you have a character in your film that is doing something, but we aren't quite sure why, THIS is your track. Packing a suitcase full of marshmallows? Half Mystery! Wiring a toaster into the side of a city bus? Half Mystery! Talking to their mother-in-law about monocot sexuality? Actually... that might be too much for this track.
credit: "Half Mystery" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hall of the Mountain King
description: Edvard Grieg's famous piece from Peer Gynt (1876). You know this piece.  Starts quiet - ends loud. This is a "cinematic mix" that is a little sharper than most recordings and less dynamic. Source recordings placed into the Public Domain by the MusOpen project.
credit: "Hall of the Mountain King" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Halls of the Undead
description: Deep dark background undercurrent.
credit: "Halls of the Undead" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hammock Fight
description: Light background... possibly for a physical comedy bit.
credit: "Hammock Fight" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hamster March
description: A snappy little tune that might have been found in the 50s.
credit: "Hamster March" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hand Balance Redux
description: Intense, slightly urban piece with rich chordal melodies.
credit: "Hand Balance Redux" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

description: Lively yet quiet barroom-style ditty.
credit: "Hand Trolley" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Happy Alley" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Happy Bee
description: Fun little organ based super light rock tune with some 1950's sensibilities.
credit: "Happy Bee" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Happy Boy End Theme" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

description: Happy bouncy theme for a comic hero! Written for Craig Knitt's short "Happy Boy".
credit: "Happy Boy Theme" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Happy Happy Game Show
description: Okay, it is a 12 bar blues, but you got to stick around at least until the horns! I couldn't start with the horns as that would be a frightening level of happy. The uncompressed download also comes with a perfectly loopable track for those who don't want the party to end.
credit: "Happy Happy Game Show" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hard Boiled
description: You're looking for the low-down, huh? That's going to take lettuce.  You want the dope? the scoop? the skinny? Ten bucks a day plus expenses. No negotiations. I ain't no fourth-rate gumshoe - but a ducky shincracker like you already knew that... Out of curiosity, what's the word for people who overuse slang?
credit: "Hard Boiled" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Harlequin
description: Quirky little duet. Major contrast between a staccato piano line, and the sweeping long bass clarinet.
credit: "Harlequin" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Harmful or Fatal
description: Electronica (techo, light industrial). This one moves with a crazy speed guitar doubling some synth lines, and making some lines or its own. Harsh.
credit: "Harmful or Fatal" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Healing
description: Mostly pentatonic piece. Listening may cause healing of undisclosed issues.
credit: "Healing" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

description: Lush vocals and calming chords.
credit: "Heart of Nowhere" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Heart of the Beast

credit: "Heart of the Beast" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Heartbreaking

credit: "Heartbreaking" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Heartwarming
description: Quick and flowing like water, the piano is warm and bright, perfect for a romantic comedy or tender interlude. The melody is sweet and repeated four times in different refrains. First at the main register, then an octave lower at 0:12. After the bridge interlude at 0:23, the melody resumes at 0:35, and at 0:49 plays in a higher register, then slows to the final arpeggiated resolve.
credit: "Heartwarming" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Heavy Heart
description: We've all been there. It is a little sad, a little hopeful... like when you finally set your rescue owl back into the world. You're sad to see her go, but you hope for the best. You've done all you can inside... her wings work pretty well now, and she can snatch the mice from your living room floor even when you put in a bunch of fake plants in the way to give the prey cover. Nothing to do now but hope Blossom can rule the night as you hoped she one day would. Also... time to buy a bunch of mousetraps.
credit: "Heavy Heart" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Heavy Interlude
description: A short, bouncy, medieval sounding piece with heavy use of Bouzouki and Hammer Dulcimer.  Strings used in the background, main melody carried by Violin and Hammer Dulcimer.
credit: "Heavy Interlude" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hep Cats
description: Going to the grocery store? Need a theme for that? Maybe you've got a swank cocktail party that needs some swank music? All of these things are possible and more with this upbeat organ-based piece!
credit: "Hep Cats" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hero Down
description:
A piece in three or four parts... depending on how you count parts. The penultimate section features a lonely flute, slowly joined by a children's choir, and finally exploding into a giant choral and orchestral ending.

 From the original soundtrack to "The Last Stand of the Mechanolith".
credit: "Hero Down" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hero Theme
description: A short, powerful theme with a bit of hope.
credit: "Hero Theme" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Heroic Age
description: See title, instrumentation, tempo, and feels for description. Originally written for a live performance.

credit: "Heroic Reception" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hidden Agenda
description: Intimate sneaking around sort of music. Many breaks and hits allow for re-editing to suit the scene.
credit: "Hidden Agenda" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hidden Past
description: Pipes, pipes, and more pipes! Irish? Scottish? Celtic? I have no idea. But sure - could be any of those. Let's call it "Ancient British Isles".
credit: "Hidden Past" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hidden Wonders
description: Would you like to sample my wares? I specialize in non-djinn-infested housewares! Djinn-free spoons, Djinn-free curtains, Djinn-free spices, mostly Djinn-free oil lamps, Djinn-free flying carpets (still magic, but not Djinn powered). Come on in to Gazeem's Discount mostly-Djinn-free Housewares Tent! You won't be disappointed... unless you want a Djinn, then go see Maghrib.
credit: "Hidden Wonders" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hiding Your Reality
description: It hurts my brain to switch from english words to symbols. Try to read these words and symbols out loud quickly: hyphen-slash-backslash/dash/-\hyphen//hashtag_octothorpe#- Crazy, right? That had nothing to do with this piece of music. I'm just sharing.
credit: "Hiding Your Reality" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Highlight Reel
description: Not pure rock, it has jazz and funk characteristics. Reminds me of the under music for a sports highlights telecast. Rock beat, a few guitars, and a nice electric bass.
credit: "Highlight Reel" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Hillbilly Swing" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Himalayan Atmosphere" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Hitman" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Holiday Weasel" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

description: Short loopable piece meant for a video game section.
credit: "Home Base Groove" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Honey Bee
description: The electric piano alternates between playing the rhythm and creating a sliding melody, while trumpets sound in the background, sometimes stealing the melody. The percussion makes for a toe-tapping good time. This is useful for the closing segment of a TV show, game, or transition. Cleanly loopable.
credit: "Honey Bee" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hot Pursuit
description: RUN! It is the Hemiola Monster!!!! We just need to get to the bar! It doesn't seem to want to cross the bar! Oh my GOD! It has friends!! No wait, that's just a standard clave pattern...  (no, I'm not explaining this description OR what is wrong with my head.)
credit: "Hot Pursuit" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hot Swing
description: A nice upbeat swing tune with a change-up in the middle, and big ending.
credit: "Hot Swing" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hotrock
description: Power guitar rock with a 4-piece horn section.
credit: "Hotrock" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: How it Begins
description: Rounded quantized synths with a happy happy backbeat. This is quite happy.
credit: "How it Begins" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hush
description: Creepy little piece with a buildup and action hit around 1:30.
credit: "Hush" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hustle
description: The bass guitar plays a familiar rolling Blues riff, while accompanied by organ, acoustic guitar, and drums. A toe-tapping beat plays throughout, and can be used as the background music for a fast-paced game or scene, or as the intro to a scene full of bustling people.
credit: "Hustle" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Hyperfun
description: Some ragtime, some western saloon piano, all fun. More fun than you can handle. That's HYPERfun!
credit: "Hyperfun" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
