credit: "Hypnothis" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: I Can Feel it Coming
description: Just your average, run-of-the-mill tension filler music... Or IS it!? Yeah, it pretty much is. This does feature a poorly played guitar synth, though... so it is a stand-out in that way. If you were here for tension-building music, you already have this piece... Move along.
credit: "I Can Feel it Coming" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: I Feel You
description: A sort of backgroundy 1980's-ish dreamy rock fusion thingee.
credit: "I Feel You" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: I Got a Stick Arr Bryan Teoh
description: Funky Horns? Funk!  Funky Guitar? Funk!  Funky Bass? Funk!  Funky Drumming? Double Funk!!  Arrangement and instruments: Bryan Teoh
credit: "I Got a Stick Arr Bryan Teoh" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: I Got a Stick Feat James Gavins
description: Funky Horns? Funk!  Funky Guitar? Funk!  Funky Bass? Funk!  Funky Drumming? Double Funk!!  Vocals: James Gavins. Uncopyrightable Lyrics: ("I got a stick.") James Gavins and Kevin MacLeod Arrangement and instruments: Bryan Teoh
credit: "I Got a Stick Feat James Gavins" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: I Knew a Guy
description: Slow walking bass, drums follow along sparely, with a cool Vibe melody.
credit: "I Knew a Guy" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ibn Al-Noor
description: Evocative of the Arab world, the music begins stoically; the melody accentuated by simple percussive sounds. Within the first minute, the strings hypnotize with their sinuous melody, the tribal drumming awakening the senses. In the third minute the piece changes to a heavy, dangerous string and tribal drumming that builds until all of the instruments come together in a fitful way, until the abrupt ending.
credit: "Ibn Al-Noor" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ice Demon
description: Hollow creepy background pad. This is not the feel-good hit of the summer. It is more like the cheese-grater to the brain of uncomfortableness.
credit: "Ice Demon" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ice Flow
description: This is another piece where the Feel descriptors don't work all that well. This is a sort of urban chill mix.
credit: "Ice Flow" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ignosi
description: Starts without percussion, then adds in a groove later on.
credit: "Ignosi" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Immersed
description: Minimal and somewhat droney in parts, this has a beautiful calmness about it. You can use it to sell anti-depressants or high performance automobile parts. Also useful for time-lapse photography of the night sky... or maybe a rocket launch.
credit: "Immersed" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Impact Allegretto
description: Track 5 of 6. Percussion starts on the offbeat. Large shift at 34 seconds, building to another at 42 seconds. Additional shift to mostly percussion at 1:52. Good pacing contours.
credit: "Impact Allegretto" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Impact Andante
description: 2 of 6. This piece changes perspectives a few times, and stays very fresh throughout.
credit: "Impact Andante" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Impact Intermezzo
description: 4 of 6. Zero melody, all percussion piece... might be useful for anything that needs a bit of urgency, but not too much.
credit: "Impact Intermezzo" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Impact Lento
description: 6 of 6. Very slow start. This piece uses warm but thin textures, and several striking chord progressions.
credit: "Impact Lento" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Impact Moderato
description: 3 of 6. Laid back drum kit with a lot of extra percussion under a simple guitar.
credit: "Impact Moderato" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Impact Prelude
description: 1 of 6. Chill opening theme with lots of percussion bits.
credit: "Impact Prelude" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Impending Boom
description: That sort of tension music for when people are trying to diffuse a bomb. Has other uses as well. Sixteenth notes beginning to end.
credit: "Impending Boom" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Impromptu in Blue
description: Impromptu performed on a Steinway Model D tuned to Quarter Comma Meantone. In this piece the most out-of-tune notes give it a feel that is not often heard in contemporary piano music.
credit: "Impromptu in Blue" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Impromptu in Quarter Comma Meantone
description: Impromptu performed on a Steinway Model D tuned to Quarter Comma Meantone. This gives a very rich feel to the base chords, but leaves a couple of "wolf notes" in the gaps (most notably in the Ab). 2 minutes in, it lingers on the most out-of tune part of the scales.
credit: "Impromptu in Quarter Comma Meantone" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: In a Heartbeat
description: Electronica (industrial dance). Hard, hard, super-hard, gritty, you-had--better-want-to-be-angry electronica. This piece is fast and harsh.
credit: "In a Heartbeat" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: In The West
description: The percussion and strings start off bright, but deceive you as they turn to a powerful minor key. The string bass plays a prominent role, interacting with and leading the treble to the sudden conclusion.
credit: "In The West" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: In Your Arms
description: A piece of music from a more elegant time, 1940. This is a beautiful slow piece that will make you want to pick up some champagne and go off slow dancing with people... or penguins. I like penguins. And now some searchable words: Big Band. 1940s. Forties. Formal Party. Penguin Slow Dance. No Whammies.
credit: "In Your Arms" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Industrial Cinematic
description: The Year: Future Year. The planet has been ravaged by desertification... that apparently no one saw coming... Not sure how that happened, I mean Jeez! Anyone ever hear of a little disaster called "The Aral Sea"? That seriously screwed up... like... everything. I guess the dam is supposed to help, but I'm seriously not holding my breath. Oh. Industrial-sounding music.
credit: "Industrial Cinematic" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Industrial Music Box
description: Music box with 2 ranks of tines, and one set of bells.
credit: "Industrial Music Box" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Industrial Revolution
description: A sort of steampunk industrial piece with a lovely melody.
credit: "Industrial Revolution" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Industrious Ferret
description: How bustling do Gnomish villages get? I imagine not more bustling than this.  If I were a gnome.... out there bustling my butt every day, this would be my soundtrack.
credit: "Industrious Ferret" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Inexorable
description: Highly processed and oddly played piano makes up the harmonic base of this piece. Sort sort of ticking clock thing... This is a brash mix, but probably not as bad as you think!
credit: "Inexorable" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Infados
description: Thins out at 1:30, then adds in and accelerates, dropping back down for another build. Abrupt ending.
credit: "Infados" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Infinite Perspective
description: All the beauty, awe and calm majesty you can handle... without a permit or prescription medication. The download comes with a faster and slower bonus tempo as well as the original sketch on marimba that was used in making this piece!
credit: "Infinite Perspective" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Inner Light
description: A chill, reverb-drenched romantic piece in 6/8
credit: "Inner Light" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Inner Sanctum
description: Glimmering darkness with some smooth emergences and some sharp. Spectrally, this is all over the place. It creeps me out.
credit: "Inner Sanctum" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Inspired
description: Quite a broad piece. Could be used for corporate films of intricate industrial processes, or a flashback scene to the time at the lake a few summers ago. Maybe good background to your cousin's magic show at the last family reunion. Or a film where you do "industrial processes" at the "lake" with your "cousin". It is really quite versatile!
credit: "Inspired" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Interloper
description: Multi-part cue that builds as it accelerates.
credit: "Interloper" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Intractable
description: Probably best classified as light-funk. Chorused bass line.
credit: "Intractable" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Intrepid
description: This has a little bit of early music flair to it with a nice vocal performance (if you don't like the vocals, you can get a version without in the super download). I've listened to this piece non-stop for like an hour. Still beautiful! The least you could do is listen to this once! It is only a few minutes. Go ahead!
credit: "Intrepid" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Intuit
description: I chose the sound palate, and then assembled the piece without listening to it. The interesting bit is that it was assembled visually - looking at the waveform profiles. This is my first one, and the sound selections are all amiable. I am unsure of the genre. Trance?
credit: "Intuit" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Invariance
description: One file that contains the same piece in 2 tempos; slower and faster. The slower version gives a more tribal feel - the fast one destroys that, and lends a slight edge-of-the-seat feel.
credit: "Invariance" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Investigations
description: Sort of a loafing comedic piece for all of your amusing scenes with dialog that does not need to move the story. Also reasonable for scenes with no dialog.
credit: "Investigations" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Iron Bacon
description: Mid-tempo rockin' tune from the fictional band Glory Nugget. Can they play? Absolutely not. It is awesome? Absolutely.
credit: "Iron Bacon" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Iron Horse
description: Darkly plodding, this staccato piano piece is the tense setting for the classic silent film scene: the heroine is tied to the train tracks, the steam engine train plugging along towards her. The chug-a-chug feel is maintained by a tense hammering of the chords in triplets, depicting machinery or chaos set in motion without an end in sight.
credit: "Iron Horse" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Iron Horse - Distressed
description: Darkly plodding, this staccato piano piece is the tense setting for the classic silent film scene: the heroine is tied to the train tracks, the steam engine train plugging along towards her. The chug-a-chug feel is maintained by a tense hammering of the chords in triplets, depicting machinery or chaos set in motion without an end in sight.
credit: "Iron Horse - Distressed" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ishikari Lore
description: A new piece derived from Eastern folk music.
credit: "Ishikari Lore" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Island Meet and Greet
description: While this is a party, we caution all the lemmings out there against the formation of conga lines. Things can, and have, taken a turn for the tragic out by the cliffs, volcanos, quicksand pits, coconut groves, tidal pools, and most tragic of all… the gift shop.
credit: "Island Meet and Greet" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Isolated
description: Intricate finger styling on a bass guitar creates a thematic melody full of solitude that drastically slows to a lethargic ending. This makes for a great transition piece for an outdoors scene or to depict isolation.
credit: "Isolated" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: It Came Upon a Midnight Clear
description: You know that touching Christmas slideshow you're working on? This is for that.
credit: "It Came Upon a Midnight Clear" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: It is Lost
description: Highly melodic pad with a sense of fleeting hope.
credit: "It is Lost" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Itty Bitty 8 Bit
description: Playful and interesting, Itty Bitty 8-Bit immediately introduces you to a pulsating melody flitting above a synthesized bass. The melody changes in the second minute and builds while climbing the chromatic scale, before settling back into the familiar refrain. This could be looped for a classic-styled videogame that is quirky and imaginative.
credit: "Itty Bitty 8 Bit" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Jalandhar
description: Super groovy Indian-inspired piece with a chill bass line, and amazing percussion.
credit: "Jalandhar" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Jaunty Gumption
description: Mid-90s styled happy happy video game music.
credit: "Jaunty Gumption" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Jazz Brunch
description: This is the music playing at the slightly-too-nice cafe - while you pretend to be rational while discussing who gets to keep which snakes in the divorce. I mean, the snakes don't really seem to care... they just hang out in the drawers most of the time. And you kind of really want to keep Alice, the piebald ball python... she's really photogenic, but she is kind of a jerk.
credit: "Jazz Brunch" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Jellyfish in Space
description: This is somewhat relaxing, while still having some forward momentum. Kind of like sleeping on a train... or taking MBA classes. I like the spinney-sounding synths. The chorus effects give this piece a watery feel. Kind of like a shimmering pond... or being on hold for an insurance company run by sperm whales.
credit: "Jellyfish in Space" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Jerry Five
description: Sort of a cooler, driving piece. Lots of space in this piece to make it your own. I don't mean "make it your own" in that sort of way you do where you mark all the pancakes on your plate with your signature so you can tell if someone switched out your pancakes while you weren't looking. Honestly that's pretty weird.Who could possibly want to switch out your pancakes? I mean - who thinks like that? Sure, everyone NOW wants to screw with your pancakes, but before you started all of this - it wouldn't have crossed one person's mind! NOT ONE!
credit: "Jerry Five" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring
description: This is a truncated version of BWV 147. J. S. Bach.
credit: "Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Jet Fueled Vixen
description: Griggs! I've been poisoned! You gotta get me the antidote! Then you gotta get... like a crane, or something to lift this truck off me! She dropped a truck on me, Griggs!!! Then, if you could find me a decent deal on high speed internet - that would be great! The plans are all too confusing, and I do NOT WANT CABLE TV OR TELEPHONES! Can you believe anyone still has telephones, Griggs? Griggs??!!?
credit: "Jet Fueled Vixen" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Jingle Bells
description: Happy, clappy arrangement worthy of a 6th grade band program.
credit: "Jingle Bells" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Jingle Bells (Calm)
description: Quite a calm arrangement of a piece that should probably be more joyous. Slow and free. This isn't really a sing-along type recording.
credit: "Jingle Bells (Calm)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Joey's Formal Waltz - Scented
description: It's your Grade 10 Formal and no one is dancing. All the usual cliques are in all the usual places, and questions are spinning around in your head... Would Alex actually dance with me? How can I make that happen? What's that smell? Did I wear deodorant? What exactly do I do with my left hand!? How big IS the Holy Ghost!???  It is my sincerest wish that this piece be requested at every high-school aged formal dance, for obvious reasons.  Also available in unscented.
credit: "Joey's Formal Waltz - Scented" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Joey's Formal Waltz - Unscented
description: There are NO FARTS in this version. If you're looking for farts, you want the "Scented" version.  Just your average, repeated, beautiful slow waltz with some chill EP and electric guitar.  Also available with fart sounds.
credit: "Joey's Formal Waltz - Unscented" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Journey To Ascend
description: Jamming on some cheap percussion with some friends and a click track.  Recommended uses for this track: Tiki bar, Museum exhibit of a bear,  On hold music for an adventure bike tour company, Street festival in Monrovia (Liberia - not California).
credit: "Journey To Ascend" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Juniper
description: Themes, rhythms, chords all stolen from Holst.
credit: "Juniper" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Junkyard Tribe
description: Accelerating piece of contemporary electronic percussions. There's some bit crusting going down, and a few other things. No melodies - just the hits.
credit: "Junkyard Tribe" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Just As Soon
description: Slow 6/8. Did you ever get up in the middle of the night and wonder what would happen if you took a Spanish guitar player, tell them to do a ballad, and give them a tasteful jazz quartet? I did.
credit: "Just As Soon" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Just Nasty
description: A driving funk piece that is sometimes distorted because it plays with clashing grooves. EP prominent throughout the entire piece. Kit mainly in the background. Horn section accompanies EP in several places, however is not used equally throughout.
credit: "Just Nasty" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Kalimba Relaxation Music
description: Can you believe kalimbas are only like $20? Check them out in my amazon affilliate store! (I do not have an amazon affiliate store.)
credit: "Kalimba Relaxation Music" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Kawai Kitsune
description: A very electronic semi-soothing piece of bleeps and bloops! I originally wrote this piece to be calm, but in the uncompressed download, there are a couple of faster versions! YOU CANNOT CONTAIN THE EXCITEMENT!
credit: "Kawai Kitsune" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Keystone Deluge
description: This piece has 3 major sections, all of which are large and violent.
credit: "Keystone Deluge" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Kick Shock
description: Poppy electronic dance piece, thick with synths and phasing.  Strong lead synth melody in beginning, ends with exposed drum part.
credit: "Kick Shock" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Killers
description: This piece starts BIG. Originally, this piece started slowly and built... and then I got bored and chopped out all the slowness. There are still dynamics, but if you need bigness from the get-go - here's what you get! Vroom! BIG BIG BIG! Could be too big. Could be. Probably isn't.
credit: "Killers" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Killing Time
description: Super bright super tight electronic mix with a beat turn-around around 2 minutes in, followed by swirling synths.
credit: "Killing Time" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Kings of Tara
description: This one is just cool. If you just tried to dance to this and fell over, that's because every measure is missing one beat. Still it grooves quite well, assuming you can groove in 7/4 time. Uncompressed download comes with individual tracks so you can make your own mixes.
credit: "Kings of Tara" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Klockworx
description: This piece is in a genre sort of made by an electronic instrument from Yamaha called the Tenori-On (though it was not made on one of them). It is a sixteenth note-quantized all-synth 4 bar repeated thing. Items are only added, never removed.
credit: "Klockworx" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Kool Kats
description: A sort of simple lounge chill spy piece.
credit: "Kool Kats" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Krampus Workshop
description: Is it looking a little claymation in here, or is it just me?
credit: "Krampus Workshop" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Kumasi Groove
description: Small drum ensemble based loosely on west African styles. This one is pretty laid back. Tumba/Conga/Quinto/Marimba/Shakers/etc.
credit: "Kumasi Groove" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Kumasi Groove (plus flugelhorn)
description: Small drum ensemble based loosely on west African styles. This version also features a be-bop flugelhorn solo. Tumba/Conga/Quinto/Marimba/Shakers/etc.
credit: "Kumasi Groove (plus flugelhorn)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Lachaim
description: Klezmer band arrangement.
credit: "Lachaim" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Laconic Granny
description: Lumbering tuba-driven tune with heavy back beat appropriate for character underscore. Ends Abruptly.
credit: "Laconic Granny" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Lagoa v1
description: Brazilian carnival style samba music. This is the most chill of the pieces I've made in this style.
credit: "Lagoa v1" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Lagoa v2
description: Brazilian carnival style music at an aggressive tempo. It is not possible to be unhappy listening to this.
credit: "Lagoa v2" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Laid Back Guitars
description: An experiment in reverb. The piece itself has two Spanish guitars with lots of different percussion backings. The congas are definitely reverb-affected more noticeably than the bells or cymbals.
credit: "Laid Back Guitars" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Lamentation
description: Slow solo harp piece.
credit: "Lamentation" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Land of Phantoms
description: More a creepy orchestral percussive soundscape than a piece of music with melody and harmony. That thing you can't identify is a gong being played abnormally.
credit: "Land of Phantoms" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Land of the Dead
description: A background pad full of human souls. A cacophony of choirs run in counter directions. This is very unpleasant to listen to at volume.
credit: "Land of the Dead" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Laser Groove
description: It came from the 1980s, but was mutated by some trap monster which gave it a new lease on life! I'm not gonna lie, this is an odd hybrid - super useful for your YouTube channels! You can't not like this piece... unless you have no soul.
credit: "Laser Groove" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Laserpack
description: Hey, man! Is that an Atoke? Hells yeah, its an Atoke! If I could choose of any shape of percussion - I’m going to choose "Taco-shaped percussion". There is no other feeling quite like beating your metal taco with a stick. I wish this description were more fictional than it actually is.
credit: "Laserpack" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Last Kiss Goodnight
description: Classic 50's/60's I, iv, IV, V chord progression as in "Unchained Melody" or "Sleepwalk".
credit: "Last Kiss Goodnight" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Lasting Hope
description: Minimal percussion gives a subtle edge to the smooth synth line.
credit: "Lasting Hope" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Late Night Radio
description: You know when you're at a friend's house overnight for an experimental airplane convention and there are people sleeping on various sofas, so you don't want to turn on the lights - but then you run your shin smack into the metal coffee table, knocking over 3 mostly empty bottles and somehow breaking your friends glasses? This music is the nice feeling before the coffee table incident.
credit: "Late Night Radio" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Latin Industries
description: Halting electronic dance piece that ends with a giant lush finale.
credit: "Latin Industries" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Le Grand Chase
description: You never notice how effective a car horn is until you use it. I usually park my car near a sidewalk and alarm 7 year olds on their way to and from school. 7 year olds are your target market for this sort of thing. They jump like antelope! All the kids in my neighborhood are acclimatized, now. It isn't as much fun. You also never notice how effective a Picardy third is until you do it with car horns. You're welcome.
credit: "Le Grand Chase" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Leaving Home
description: Ukulele and flutes and glockenspiel... I think you already know what this sounds like. The percussion is also adorable.
credit: "Leaving Home" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Leblon
description: Mid-up-tempo Brazilian carnival style piece. ABA form.
credit: "Leblon" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Legend of One
description: Dark electronic piece with piano carrying the interest.
credit: "Legend of One" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Leopard Print Elevator
description: Smooth. Seriously smooth. Smooth like you can't even imagine how smooth this is. Still has a lot of life, though! The uncompressed download comes with an alternate mix with a super deep electric bass for even more smoothness! Did I mention it is smooth? Sort of like an early 1970's era vibe to it. But smoother.
credit: "Leopard Print Elevator" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Level Up

title: Long Time Coming
description: Tense and mercurial, ?Long Time Coming? begins with a slow, frenetic crescendo, and at 0:40 builds into the main melody with heavy percussion. At 1:04 the percussion is tacit, and at 1:18 a rippling crescendo builds to long, demented pulls on the string bass. The percussive beat begins again at 2:18, and then the frenzied, reverbed staccato of the piano enters, accompanied by a swelling synth lead. At 3:40 the piece finds it?s stride with pulsating synthesizer effects and a rumbling bass line. Best used as accompaniment for a tense, difficult level of a game or as the final battle with a villain. Because of its steady bass beat and snyth effects, this could also work well to depict a tense and suspenseful race to the finish, or as the music playing during a vibrant, pounding rave.
credit: "Long Time Coming" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

It never happened! That was a screen memory! There are no centaurs, and they wouldn't live in forest settlements! That was an alien abduction. The aliens planted the memory of the forest centaurs so your brain wouldn't implode with the knowledge of trans-dimensional beings... such as themselves. And... unrelated, but... what comes to mind when you think about the smell of wet cardboard and Sriracha?

So, then you make it, and realize it should be called a "Flaccid Spiced Hummus Ball". Eating a flaccid spiced hummus ball helps to assess your life choices... that eventually led you to eating a flaccid spiced hummus ball.  Uncompressed download comes in 4 speeds; 72, 80 (this one), 88, and 96 beats per minute. Flaccid spiced hummus ball.

title: Merry Go Slower
description: Comedic and playful, this rag-time ditty has a strong melody, and is heavy in the bass chords. The second minute features flighty finger-work, as if an energetic bee is flying up and down the scales. The last thirty seconds is a refrain of the introduction, and the piece ends with an invigorating flourish.
credit: "Merry Go Slower" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Merry Go Slower - Distressed
description: Comedic and playful, this rag-time ditty has a strong melody, and is heavy in the bass chords. The second minute features flighty finger-work, as if an energetic bee is flying up and down the scales. The last thirty seconds is a refrain of the introduction, and the piece ends with an invigorating flourish.
credit: "Merry Go Slower - Distressed" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mesmerize
description: Need to suck someone in? This piece never quite gives what you want.... so you just get sucked in. Perfect for videos like: Disassembling a watch, Removing a giant zit, Drilling a hole in a glacier, or anything that takes just a little longer than most people think it should.
credit: "Mesmerize" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mesmerizing Galaxy
description:
This piece was written for a 2d-bullet-hell space shooter. It loops seamlessly to allow variable-length gameplay. There is no percussion because of all the explosions in the game itself. The piece probably has some utility beyond bullet-hell; paranormal investigation comes to mind. If you are doing paranormal investigations, I would like to see the following shows: 
 -"Ghosts of the Galaxy"
 -"The Otherworld Unit"
 -"Whispers from the Unknown"
 -"Unearthly Encounters"
 -"Phantom Photons"
These would also make excellent science/astronomy shows.
credit: "Mesmerizing Galaxy" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Metalmania
description: I was doing some research on metal... today's description is going to involve some participation on your part. Step 1) Google: "Death Metal English" the first link should be from invisibleoranges. Step 2) Enjoy!  You're welcome.
credit: "Metalmania" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Metaphysik
description: Slow, odd, and gosh-darned beautiful! There's a lot of subtle droniness and reverses. Maybe something supernatural here? There is certainly some things that aren't right about it.
credit: "Metaphysik" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Miami Nights - Extended Theme
description: Did you ever wake up one day and think, "I should write an entire soundtrack treatment for a reboot of an early 90s tv action-drama that will probably never get produced!" Of course you didn't. No worries. I got you. If they do reboot "Miami Vice," I want to capture the crappy synthetic feel of the era, but with more natural sound. There are drum machines in here that were placed on a stage, put through amps, recorded on microphones, then digitally processed to sound more like drum machines. You’re welcome.
credit: "Miami Nights - Extended Theme" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Miami Viceroy
description: Musical wallpaper! You might think that's a bad thing, but it quite useful for playing under interviews, or during countdowns, or in really hip cafes where you can get an Americano (coffee) or an Americano (Campari+vermouth cocktail). Life Pro Tip: ALWAYS refrigerate your vermouth! It is a wine product and will go bad if open at room temperature. So, to all of you who "hate vermouth", no - you hate ruined vermouth. Just like anyone who has only had room temperature red wine that's been opened for 3 weeks would hate wine.
credit: "Miami Viceroy" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Midday Dance
description: Impromptu piano solo with a strange little bounce rhythm. Catchy, and slightly "off". Ends on a fat rich chord.
credit: "Midday Dance" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Midnight Meeting
description: Pipe organ mini-fuge.
credit: "Midnight Meeting" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Midnight Tale
description: Gather 'round the tavern's fire and I will share a tale for as long as I have ale. Hah! "Tale and ale!" I'm not guaranteeing rhymes, though. That was a coincidence. I was playing lute for an uninterested group of tavern-goers, when all of a sudden, I remembered that I had a sandwich for lunch! It looks like I'm out of ale, so that is the end of my tale.
credit: "Midnight Tale" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Midsummer Sky
description: Solo new-age piano.
credit: "Midsummer Sky" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mighty and Meek
description: An epic piece involving lots of parallel chordal movement.  All Horns throughout. Trumpets used mainly for the fanfare type bits.
credit: "Mighty and Meek" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mighty Like Us
description: Only 6 monophonic synths and a drum set in this entire, extremely peppy, undeniably enthusiastic, off-kilter, oddly satisfying electronic piece! Even at that, it gets pretty dense near the end.   Try this one! You'll like it! (you'll probably like it... figure about 90 percent guaranteed to like this piece by the end.) The uncompressed download comes with a mix done using electronic drums. It has a very different and more machine-like feel. Chances you'll like that one are lower... but it is totally usable for a harsher feel.
credit: "Mighty Like Us" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Militaire Electronic
description: Snare line with quads and a bass line add marching flair for an electronic groove.
credit: "Militaire Electronic" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mind Scrape
description: Interesting collection of consonant and dissonant sounds across the spectrum of sound.
credit: "Mind Scrape" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Minima
description:
The orchestra is woodwind-heavy, it is actually low-winds-heavy so You've got a lot of Contrabass Clarinet,  Bass Clarinet, Contra Bassoon, Bassoon... And they're just pulsing... Pulsing and pulsing and pulsing.
 So what do you use this for? I don't know. Some things that aren't quite real. It's not a very real-sounding thing.
credit: "Minima" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mining by Moonlight
description: Light, upbeat, cool - useful for video game montages, and telephone on-hold music... and... nearly anything where you need something interesting - but not TOO interesting.
credit: "Mining by Moonlight" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Minstrel Guild
description: Music from the 1400s or thereabouts. A quite lively little piece for your town or tavern.
credit: "Minstrel Guild" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mirage
description: A sort of drone-based piece with something that sounds like a waterphone, and some other things that I don't know what they could be. Super chill - good amounts of tension with some glorious consonants.
credit: "Mirage" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Miri's Magic Dance
description: Eastern European folk-sounding dark, slowish dance.
credit: "Miri's Magic Dance" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mischief Maker
description: Hey buddy, wanna buy a ferret? How about a trained ferret? Okay, I didn't really train her... she just has a predisposition to things. She stuffs squirrels into boxes, feeds them sugary treats and then empties the boxes though mailslots. Well, if you're not going to buy her, how about some nails... to keep your mailslot closed.
credit: "Mischief Maker" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mistake the Getaway
description: The chase begins with horn blasts, and the kit plays a solid beat while the bass strings are a pulsing drone below the horn melody. The piece grows more tense and emotional, the strings taking the lead and rise into a flowing intensity. Danger returns in full force as the music crescendos and return for one final push.
credit: "Mistake the Getaway" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mister Exposition
description: bubbly ragtime piano with an occasional tuba.
credit: "Mister Exposition" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Misuse
description: Sort of a dark dance piece. Interesting things happen regularly.
credit: "Misuse" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Modern Jazz Samba
description: A nice little 85 BMP piece with guitar, piano, bass, and flute. Kind of jazzy and slightly blues-y with a more rocking beat. The bass in this piece is actually a sample from an 18th century double bass. Most latin players aren't likely to be on one of these... but it was the only one I had at the time.
credit: "Modern Jazz Samba" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Modern Vibes
description: Modern Vibraphone composition. 4 mallet, plays with rhythm over the entire range of the instrument.
credit: "Modern Vibes" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Monkeys Spinning Monkeys
description: Loopable happy light fluffy piece with bright flutes and a bunch of pizzicato strings.
credit: "Monkeys Spinning Monkeys" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Monkoto
description: Clashing time signatures, but a cohesive piece.
credit: "Monkoto" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Monster Promenade
description: "What a fun harmonic rollercoaster on the new tune!" Reminiscent of a carnival, this is an intentionally clashing harmonic piece... yet somehow very fun and quirky.
credit: "Monster Promenade" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Montauk Point
description: Unobtrusive simple guitar, bass, drums combo.
credit: "Montauk Point" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Montego
description: Modern yet classic reggae piece. Starts with a classic video game riff.
credit: "Montego" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Moon Lounge Omicron Prime
description: Okay, not quite a synth, not quite and organ - that thing is a mellotron. And it is cool. Interesting baroque changes in the B section. General Space-age cocktail party awesomeness for the entire piece.
credit: "Moon Lounge Omicron Prime" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Moonlight Beach
description: Bare bones island vibe without all the excitement and thrills. At about 2 and a half minutes in, it gets even less exciting! The mallet rolls are pretty good though. I used an EM1 Malletstation and real mallets. Makes a difference.
credit: "Moonlight Beach" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Moonlight Hall
description: 6/8 Starts nice, Ends frantic. The original melody was written to be performed on a Viol de Gamba... but I moved it over to oboe.
credit: "Moonlight Hall" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Moonstone
description: Calm sort of piece played all and only on the black keys.
credit: "Moonstone" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Moorland
description: It has Uilleann pipes, and is dark and somber. Not sure what else I can say about this.
credit: "Moorland" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Morgana Rides
description: This is dark and concerning - like the lights-out bonus level on your hidden object game. Almost exactly like that. As if it was written for the dark bonus level of a hidden object game. Just as if.
credit: "Morgana Rides" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Morning
description:
Morning. The time of day when you can’t figure out how to get to your drive-thru coffee place because there’s new construction and the sun is super low, so you’re squinting at the signs, trying to figure out if you are supposed to turn left here or if you definitely should NOT turn left here, because you will get three tires shredded by sharp, metal chunks before you fall in a hole. 

This piece of music is based on the old-timey concept of calm, beautiful, renewing mornings.
credit: "Morning" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Morocco Sting
credit: "Morocco Sting" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Motherlode
description: Big broad sound certain to give a sense of rockin' wonder! It switches back and forth between  faster guitar-driven sections and majestic horn sections. I know - it sounds like it won't work, but it totally DOES work. Just imagine motocross highlights to this! Or any extreme sport that would benefit from the use of slow motion.
credit: "Motherlode" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Motivator
description: Classic style corporate-presentation rock piece.
credit: "Motivator" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mountain Emperor
description: So many big drums! All the big drums in all one place! Bonus; Extra people banging on gamelan metals! Uncompressed download comes with a version with just the drums... I'm not sure if this of for non-musicologists who may not like the gamelan - or specifically for musicologists who think I've used the gamelan improperly.
credit: "Mountain Emperor" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mourning Song
description: Long broad notes with a solo oboe.
credit: "Mourning Song" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Move Forward
description: Mid-90s styled happy happy video game music.
credit: "Move Forward" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Movement Proposition
description: Fight scenes and chase scenes. Also good for high energy magic shows.
credit: "Movement Proposition" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mr. Mealey's Mediocre Machine
description: Quirky light piece played lightly.
credit: "Mr. Mealey's Mediocre Machine" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: MTA
description: Urban-sounding tight piece suitable for rap or stand-alone. Some giant hits, and a cool B section in here. Mix consultant: Bryan Teoh.
credit: "MTA" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Music Box Theme
description: Very simple theme voiced in very very high and bright registers.
credit: "Music Box Theme" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Music for Funeral Home - Part 11
description: This piece works very well for an actual funeral home setting, or any solemn event. The organ is light and flutey, the chords are often meandering, but have some closure now and then. There are 11 parts in this series - totaling about 34 minutes.
credit: "Music for Funeral Home - Part 11" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Music for Manatees
description: Beautiful slow moving piece with consonant sounds punctuated by rare notes that sing out over the top... like the manatee.
credit: "Music for Manatees" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Music to Delight
description: Oh, unclassifiable... this almost makes a mockery of other unclassifiable things. The woodblock player is solid. The tambourine player... not so much. Tin whistle player is delightful!
credit: "Music to Delight" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Myst
description: Theme from "AngloZulu" expanded on, but in a more relaxed sense.
credit: "Myst" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Myst on the Moor
description: Could be the thinking music for a quiz show about the paranormal? "Where does the Sasquatch typically vacation... is it A, The High Mountains... B, Unexplored Cave Systems...  C, Graceland... or D, In another dimension - similar to, but not strongly coupled with our own reality. Take your time and answer whenever you're ready.... A, B, C, or D... Would you like to consult the Tarot or do an entrail reading?" I love the flute bits in this piece.
credit: "Myst on the Moor" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mysterioso March
description: Ponderous and slightly creepy.
credit: "Mysterioso March" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mystery!
description: Theme song for a 1940's style radio show. Organs, brass, and bells with effects to increase the "age". Run time is closer to one minute without the record scratches.
credit: "Mystery!" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mystery Bazaar
description: Well met, traveller! Come warm by my brazier... Is that a Djinn in your pocket, or are you just happy to see me? Hah! I have a joke with you! ...unless it is a djinn - then you must leave immediately! ...unless that would offend the djinn - then you must stay! ...unless the djinn is going to kill me - then you must leave immediately! ...unless it will save me from a fate worse than death - then you must stay! Oh good... it was an erection. Uncompressed download comes with a faster version.
credit: "Mystery Bazaar" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mystery Sax
description: Holy smoldering tenor sax, Batman!! You want to set a mood? This is your track! It just keeps building and building! The sheet music for this recording is a post-it that says "noodle in F Minor." Such is the power of a real musician! You can just give them notes like that... and get music like this!
credit: "Mystery Sax" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mystery Sting
description: Slow groove percussion under an exotic melody.
credit: "Mystery Sting" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Mystic Force
description: Vaguely exotic sounding, yet still comfortably tonal, this piece certainly falls between some cracks. Gamelan is listed as an instrument... but that's sort of like listing an orchestra as an instrument... which I sometimes do. The other thing in here is that helicon. Imagine you take a french horn (which is like 5 meters of tubes) and make it even bigger! I guess it is also the name of a mountain in Greece? I did not use the mountain in this piece.
credit: "Mystic Force" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Nano Hoedown
description: When circuits throw a party, I imagine it sounds something like this. They can be a bit hyperactive at times. The super download comes with a more calm version at 120 beats per minute, and a crazy fast version at 180 beats per minute! All three versions loop perfectly, so you can make this as long as you need it!
credit: "Nano Hoedown" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Naraina
description: Somewhere between Bollywood and club music.
credit: "Naraina" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Neo Western
description: Big drums and an exposed 'western-style' electric guitar. Lots of drums.
credit: "Neo Western" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Neolith
description: Aggressive guitars in 2 styles. The guitar mostly in the right channel has a hard gate effect on eighth notes, giving it an almost percussive drive. The one on the left is extended power chords with a hint of a major mode to them - as opposed to the traditional unqualified (open root fifth) or minor chords that you usually find in hard rock pieces. The effect is striking at times.
credit: "Neolith" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Neon Laser Horizon
description: Build your pyramid in Five easy steps! 1) Level the intended build site 2) Get your GED in architecture 3) Quarry 100 million tons of limestone from a local quarry (cubits?) 4) Learn to be a charismatic leader 5) Synergize your assets from steps 3 and 4. Congratulations, you are on your way to pyramid success! Ask about our supplementary obelisk pamphlet!
credit: "Neon Laser Horizon" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Nerves
description: The first two minutes contain many changes and shifts in tone - all intense.  The final minute is a collection of all that came before, ending in a pulse-quickening finale. This is music for an action film, or a scene that begins with tremulous anxiety and ends in a big way.
credit: "Nerves" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Nervous
description: Background horror music. Solo piano; high and out of tune.
credit: "Nervous" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Netherworld Shanty
description: A happy little discordant march with a catchy melody.
credit: "Netherworld Shanty" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: New Direction
description: A calm ambient piece using the "Trope" synth for iPhone and some miscellaneous Logic synths.
credit: "New Direction" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: New Friendly
description: The piece starts out nice, and then becomes a modulating monster about a minute in. It resolves to the initial key, and continues on. Lots of building! Very round-sounding.
credit: "New Friendly" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: New Hero in Town
description: An epic hero has arrived. Notice has been given.
credit: "New Hero in Town" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Newer Wave
description: The 80s Gallop, a rhythmic motive heard in this piece, was popularized by many synth pop bands of yesteryear. Legend has it, some of those bands may still exist - wandering the countryside in search of slap bracelets.
credit: "Newer Wave" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: News of Sorrow
description: African-influenced short piece with continuous accelerando.
credit: "News of Sorrow" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: News Theme
description: Big, Bold, piece suitable for news themes or the like.  Starts off with a Horns, which then continue throughout.  Fades out quickly. The Whip (Extended Version)
credit: "News Theme" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: NewsSting
description: Your favorite news channel from 10 years ago.
credit: "NewsSting" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Night Break
description: Edgy-sounding synths with several pulsing band-pass sweeps.
credit: "Night Break" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

So, when you find a new critter which is certainly a new species... likely a new genus... probably a new family... and seriously might be a order. It has an exoskeleton, gives birth to live young (asexually somehow?), has a beak... We recognize all those parts, but it doesn't fit anything. Might be a new phylum.

You can experience “Northern Glade” here: https://incompetech.com/games/Magic%20Scout/

title: Nouvelle Noel
description: I say! It is such a lovely brisk day! Aren't the horses lovely? I mean... look at all the horseness they have! They are scoring quite high on the horse-o-meters today! Nothing bovine on this street, Nay! ... ... ... Wait... I was trying to make a joke involving a horse's "neigh" combined with the archaic positive/negative usage of "nay". Then everything went wrong, and I said almost the opposite of the intention. So, without the joke: Picture a street where the only animals are the horsiest of horses... No cows or pigs. Okay, there are two dogs... but one of them is pretty small... and you can see a cat in one of the windows... but MOSTLY horses. If you added up the weights of all the non-horse, non-humans in the picture, they would weigh less than one horse.

Each synth has a different program running on it that triggers more notes. Fun fact: Scotland isn't a nation. It is technically an empire that claims sovereignty over Paraguay's 400k sheep and also Neptune's "shepherd" moon Despina.

title: On Hold for You
description: The tenor sax performance in this piece was done by an AI musician. The notes and chords were generated algorithmically (not by an AI). https://sites.research.google/tonetransfer  0:33 there is an amazingly smooth and correct sounding run-up.  0:50 it goes below the actual tenor sax range. I love how it extrapolated down there! 0:58 there's some leak hiss going on at 0:58. I'll call that "artistic license". 1:08 it goes quite a bit above the standard range for a tenor sax, but those notes should be available in altissimo with some fancy fingerings. 2:20 you can almost taste the spit! 2:58 it plays the same note back to back, but changes the tone of the note. Very cool.  This ToneTransfer AI Sax is amazing. Getting this level of detail in a recording with standard virtual instruments is almost impossible. AI for the win!
credit: "On Hold for You" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Onion Capers
description: Hey buddy, that is quite the sack of onions you have! If I had a sack of onions like that, I'd be happier than a tree on Arbor Day! Everyone wants to get their hand in an onion sack like that.  Me? I like a nice purple onion, but you don't get to pick favorites when you got your hand in an onion sack. A big yellow one can feel like a little purple one. You won't know 'til you pull it out, and by then you already got yourself an onion. I know most folks don't want strangers mucking about in unfamiliar onion sacks these days, so I'll be on my way. But, that is quite the sack of onions you have.  To perform the monolog "Onion Capers" at your school or event, speak the words out loud at your school or event.

The first section begins with a bright, leading to the big push of the bombastic brass. The second section, beginning at 0:52, is the same melody, but only features the piano. This section is softer and lasts 20 seconds. The final section begins at 1:17, and ends with an excited flourish.

title: Ossuary 1 - A Beginning
description: At the intersection of relaxation and horror lies "The Ossuary". This piece is a slow-moving edgy drone with an ethereal melody on top. Since this is sort of a new genre, I'm not exactly sure where it is appropriate. Maybe a vampire spa? Dinner music for a psychopath? You'll figure it out!
credit: "Ossuary 1 - A Beginning" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ossuary 2 - Turn
description: At the intersection of relaxation and horror lies "The Ossuary".  Part 2: Turn More aggressive than part one, something is most certainly going down here. Perfect for; seeing how far down the rabbit hole goes, Loch Ness expeditions, videos about giant capacitors, dinner parties where you want everyone uncomfortable. Gets quite awful around the 3:15 mark. Awful in a good way.
credit: "Ossuary 2 - Turn" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ossuary 3 - Words

There's some amount of technology under this thing. The synth is quickly overtaken by the bizarre drones. Perfect for; being stranded in space... in a ship.
credit: "Ossuary 3 - Words" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ossuary 4 - Animate
description: At the intersection of relaxation and horror lies "The Ossuary".  Part 4: Animate It is coming for us!!!! ARGH!!!!! RUN! But where!?? Doesn't matter! Try running at the walls!!! No good! They're solid!! Is it still coming!? ARGH! Yup! There it is!!!! Now where!? The ladder!? NO GOOD COMES FROM CLIMBING A LADDER! You should know that by now! It'll just break halfway up OR something will grab your ankle OR BOTH! Just save yourself! There's no good us both getting eaten by that thing!!! Oh! And when you fill out the survey - this holiday was "VERY DISAPPOINTING!"
credit: "Ossuary 4 - Animate" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Passing Action

The reverberating congas, triangle, and synthesized percussion enhance the senses, while the bass guitar provides a strong groove. The strings raise in pitch, evoking a sense of building tension. High-pitched crescendo of strings at 0:45 is the climax of the suspense.

description: We all need sadness sometimes. I have a sadness Loot-Box subscription. This month, I got some get-well cards for babies, wilted iceberg lettuce, a 1999 Gateway laptop, 3 popped balloons, and a die-hard Montreal Expos fan. The service ships everything in an empty box of wine with a broken spigot.

title: Past the Edge
description: Slow dark and empty with a solo voice.
credit: "Past the Edge" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Peace of Mind
description: Very calm, very long piece. Piano over a drone in D.
credit: "Peace of Mind" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Peaceful Desolation" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Pensif" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Perigrine Grandeur" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

description: An interesting little piece with very organic synths and an occasional melodic flute.
credit: "Perspectives" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

Ideal for technology-induced mummy reanimation films. The alternate mixes in the full download both give a slightly different feel - one with no percussion, and one without the theremin-like synth lead.
credit: "Phantom from Space" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Phat Sketch
description: Sizzling fat analog bass line with a little beat.
credit: "Phat Sketch" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

description: Just a light piano piece for linking scenes.
credit: "Piano Between" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Piece for Disaffected Piano One
description: I hesitate to assign a 'feel' to this because it is so exotic. It uses a 19 semitone scale which does not repeat at the octave. There are 9 semitones to a perfect fifth. The tuning is Wendy Carlos' "Alpha" scale. The piano strings are laid to horrible pain in sections as two octaves of keyboard are used to represent a doubling of frequency.
credit: "Piece for Disaffected Piano One" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Piece for Disaffected Piano Two
description: Like "PfDP One", this piece also uses the Alpha scale developed by Wendy Carlos. Improvising on this piano is like walking in a minefield. There are many places to step which are just fine, but every now and again you find a surprise. This piece is light, and even comical in parts - with some musical revelations in between.
credit: "Piece for Disaffected Piano Two" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Pippin the Hunchback" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

The uncompressed download comes with a pile of extra stuff, like versions at 220, 230, 240, and a whopping 275 beats per minute! That's really fast. It also has loops that don't go through the modulation so you can repeat them as long as you'd like!

title: Pleasant Porridge

Remember to set your bleeping devices to non-bleepie mode. This show features flashing lights, live bats, and almond butter.  If you have a condition  that may cause problems, please see us at the ticket counter for further information. The show will begin shortly!

credit: "Plucky Daisy" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Political Action Ad
description: Background to an evil political action ad. Add your own alarmist voice over - this was engineered to make people uncomfortable, and not interfere with human voice range. "Tell your congressman to vote NO on the Pollute Our Drinking Water and Send All of Our Money to Canada Act."
credit: "Political Action Ad" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
