credit: "Poofy Reel" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Pookatori and Friends
description: Are your eyeballs soft? Let's be delightful with Pookatori! It is extremely happy to drink when you are thirsty. Pookatori will help! Pookatori always helps! Are you aware of your own defect? Pookatori will smile to your grandmother every day! Would you like a beautiful pie? Pookatori has many friends made from a magic and people balls. Let's have fun with Pookatori's friends! Do you like to absorbing? Functional!!
credit: "Pookatori and Friends" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Pop Goes the Weasel
description: Heavy bass drums and an string bass set the tone for this dark and menacing tone. The familiar refrain then plays, but is made expressive and almost violent as it is played on several string basses and cellos. The pace is rather quick and forceful, and after the quick ending, a jack-in-the-box plays, normally child-like, but made creepy because of the sinister music that came before.
credit: "Pop Goes the Weasel" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Poppers and Prosecco
description: What's the difference between a dead frog in the road, and a dead trombone player in the road? The frog was probably going to a gig! Hah! Get it? Well... it took me 8 years to get it, so let me explain. When you go out hunting frogs, that is called "gigging". Gigging is bad for a frog. When you go out playing an instrument in a band for money, that is called "gigging". Gigging is good for a trombone player... but man, you gotta be good. You pretty much need a bass player and a drummer... not many people need a trombone player, so they typically don't get many gigs... Did I explain that right? Wait, let me start over...
credit: "Poppers and Prosecco" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Porch Blues
description: Guitar, harmonica, piano 12 bar blues in D.
credit: "Porch Blues" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Porch Swing Days - faster
description: Acoustic guitars play a constantly flowing feel-good melody, enhanced by an airy chorus that enters early in the piece. The music is bright and evokes a carefree attitude towards life and the troubles of the world.
credit: "Porch Swing Days - faster" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Port Horizon

Other than that - not much. Except snorkeling. Snorkeling is pretty cool. Oh, there is also Art Night on Tuesday - where you get a volleyball and some paints and make yourself a friend! Beach chess... I forgot about Beach Chess. Don't play white against Todd, though - he plays all-Hedgehog all the time. Come on, Todd - just once, seriously ONCE could you play King's Indian or... you know what? I'd even take the French Defence; Exchange Variation, you boring symmetrical jerk.
credit: "Port Horizon" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Power Restored" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Prelude and Action" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

description: J. S. Bach. This is the famous first piece of the Well Tempered Clavier, Book 1. Performed on piano. Very clean recording.
credit: "Prelude in C (BWV 846)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Presenterator
description: 90s vintage presentation music with a bit more production value than the buy-out music of the day.
credit: "Presenterator" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Pride" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Private Eye

credit: "Private Eye" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Private Reflection
description: Epic myth. Part of the hero's journey. Starts with a solo soprano, and later mixes a full choir. Ends assuming you'll mix it into another piece.
credit: "Private Reflection" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Procession of the King
description: A strings only piece, evocative of love, romance, and pride. Just before the one minute mark the music takes an unexpected turn, becoming intensely emotional and beautiful as the strings play in the higher register with a slight tremolo, with the bass filling up the empty space in the last half minute.
credit: "Procession of the King" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "Professor Umlaut" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Promising Relationship
description: A striking chordal change keeps the first and second halves different.
credit: "Promising Relationship" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Protofunk
description: Lots of guitar effects built over a clean beat. Dan Ritter on guitar.
credit: "Protofunk" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

description: Harsh yet simple piece. The main theme was played with a wiimote, so don't expect too much expression! Extra interest kicks in at 1:35.
credit: "Psychedelic Crater" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Pulse
description: Nice groove in this one. Highly chorused guitar overlay.
credit: "Pulse" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Pump
description: Longer version of the fast-paced rockin' tune from the fictional band Glory Nugget. Oh yeah, it is bad, and that's what makes it great.
credit: "Pump" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Pure Attitude
description: A bouncy electronica piece heavily featuring strings and synths.
credit: "Pure Attitude" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Pyro Flow
description: You got flow? You want this. Borderline chill and aggressive, this piece is your man! It does stand alone, but if you got words... it is amazing! Try it! What style is this? I'm not sure. It borrows from a lot - but I don't think it fits anything out there. Rickenbacker bass, gnarled piano, and a distorted drum kit all fit together beautifully. Percussion breakdown at 2:17.
credit: "Pyro Flow" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Quasi Motion
description: I don't know what genre this is. Sort of Latin? Broadly? So, if you're looking for something unlike anything else... this may be it.
credit: "Quasi Motion" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Quiet Panic
description: Quiet tremolo strings that build slightly to an anti-climax.
credit: "Quiet Panic" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Quinn's Song: A New Man
description: This piece starts with piano, and ends with tymp. It uses a reharmonized theme taken from Chopin. One of 3 pieces with this theme.
credit: "Quinn's Song: A New Man" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

description: This piece contains 2 themes, one in 7/4 time, and another borrowed from Chopin - and set among very disturbing chords.

credit: "Quinn's Song: The Dance Begins" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Quirky Dog
description: Smooth and jazzy ditty with a fun edge for all your light humor needs! Okay, many of your light humor needs. Excellent for montage sequences dealing with bureaucracy.
credit: "Quirky Dog" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Radio Martini

title: Rainbows

credit: "Rainbows" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rains Will Fall
description: Slow Waltz. English Waltz. Foxtrot. Slow Fox. The piano plays a mournful, waltzing melody, while strings enter gently. Halfway into the second minute, the tone is more hopeful, but then returns to the sadness of the introduction.  Just before the third minute ends the hope returns, but melts again into sadness with the final high note of the piano. This is music for a rainy day, or when the hero to a story has lost his way.
credit: "Rains Will Fall" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ranz des Vaches
description: Ranz des Vaches or "Call to the Dairy Cows" is a small but famous section of the overture to William Tell by Rossini. It is most often used to depict morning or sleepiness in cartoons. Hook starts at 0:21.
credit: "Ranz des Vaches" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Raving Energy

This music is dangerously energetic and may cause paranoia, anxiety, and/or hallucinations.  Not the fun kind of hallucinations, either. These are the kind of hallucinations where ponies with 8 spider-like legs are climbing on your ceiling and walls while singing "Barbie Girl" and criticizing your overly-bland dating profile.
credit: "Raving Energy" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

The drums are barely noticeable. The other bass accompanies the root bass without ever gaining prominence. When the drums stop and the bass plays its final refrain, you can really hear how the music is refreshingly unrefined.

description: An amped up secret agent or pro wrestler theme with a thick wall of sound and a crazy drummer!
credit: "Ready Aim Fire" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Realizer
description: We would like to interrupt this announcement for a dance break!
credit: "Realizer" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Reawakening
description: Easy love theme; Useful for quiet talks.
credit: "Reawakening" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Redletter
description: High-pitched strings play above a low drone, while fuzzy noises and cymbal rolls flow throughout. The high strings crescendo and quickly cut out as if a knife sliced their throats.  A somber melody plays in the final minute, and the noises crescendo and come at you from every angle, symbolic of an attack and a gruesome finale.
credit: "Redletter" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Reformat
description: Sort of 8-bit retro video glitch. Excellent for a lightswitch rave! This piece loops perfectly. The uncompressed download comes in 140bpm and a super-hyped up 170bpm mix!
credit: "Reformat" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Reign
description: A piece in two parts. Slow piano intro, and then a giant power section at 1 minute 50 seconds in. Written for an animation piece.
credit: "Reign" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Reign Supreme
description: Big buildup at the end. So much suspense!
credit: "Reign Supreme" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Relaxing Piano Music
description: You can only title a piece Relaxing Piano Music once in your life, so you better bring it! Piano? You bet! Relaxing? Indeed! Music? Close enough! This 24-minute epic of calm is great for that chilly winter day, or lazy summer day... All the seasons! Wherever you need calm, you can get it here! Peaceful exclamation points? Yes!! All of them! De-stressing while studying for an exam? Go for this one! Doing a retrospective on the life and times of your pet chinchilla? You're welcome! All the calm! ALL THE TIME!!! Key of G. You can make your own mixes with the uncompressed downloads to only include the melodies you want if you like!
credit: "Relaxing Piano Music" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Relent
description: Sadness... so much sadness. Plaintiveness maybe? Anyhoo, very down.
credit: "Relent" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Reminiscing
description: Simple; mostly pentatonic.
credit: "Reminiscing" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Resignation
description: Short piece with a very quiet and rich piano part - the bass is barely audible, for low-end support.
credit: "Resignation" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: RetroFuture Clean
description: One of three mixes of this bouncy rock-funk piece. Same notes. Same instruments... just different mixes.
credit: "RetroFuture Clean" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: RetroFuture Dirty
description: One of three mixes of this bouncy rock-funk piece. Same notes. Same instruments... just different mixes.
credit: "RetroFuture Dirty" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: RetroFuture Nasty
description: One of three mixes of this bouncy rock-funk piece. Same notes. Same instruments... just different mixes.
credit: "RetroFuture Nasty" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Return of Lazarus
description: Horrible, horrific, creepy AF... all that stuff. Yuck! :-)
credit: "Return of Lazarus" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Return of the Mummy
description: Did you know that people in the 1800s used to make tea out of mummies they dug up in Egypt? Tea. Like the kind you drink. That is because people in the 1800s were dumb. They were so stupid, they thought seaweed was really quite interesting. Today, you would have to be a marine botanist to think seaweed is that exciting. I don't need to mention how "exciting" marine botanists are... Carl! Finding some Caulerpa 20 kilometers outside its published range is no reason to write a paper! And it is certainly no reason to be LATE for your OWN PARTY, CARL!!!
credit: "Return of the Mummy" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Reunited
description: Super-sappy well-executed little theme. Really opens up at 38 seconds.
credit: "Reunited" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Revival
description: So you're thinking of doing a revival tour, but you don't have a band to back up your inspirational speech? Good news, good news indeed. This piece starts very thin, and builds a couple of times.
credit: "Revival" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rhinoceros
description: Semi-8 bit, sort of 1980's synth pop crazy thing! Super energy; Crazy fun. Perfect for: automobile reviews, actions montages, martial arts clips, or anything with fast edits that needs a good pace!
credit: "Rhinoceros" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Right Behind You
description: Breathy noises make the hairs on the back of your neck stand, while screeching strings and high-pitched noises are distracting and spine-tingling.
credit: "Right Behind You" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ripples
description: Flowing like water, this serene piece is perfect for relaxation and meditation. The solitary plucks of the Chinese guzheng reverberate slightly, and maintain a steadiness that would work well for introspective, Asian-themed content. This would also work well for anything depicting snow, winter, or Rural Japan.
credit: "Ripples" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Riptide
description: Straight-up two guitar rock with a few variations. Good background... not the kind of things you'd sit and listen to on its own merit.
credit: "Riptide" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rising
description: Heavy on the percussion, this piece is dominated by the rising strings in the second minute, which quickly give way to an ethereal alto chorus. The accompaniment rises together before dissipating. Loopable.
credit: "Rising" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rising Game
description: Dark piece in 2 roughly equal main parts. Gets progressively more exciting.
credit: "Rising Game" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rising Tide
description: Let's be fair, if your interview segment was already energetic, you  don't need something like this to fix it. Most people suck at interviews. It isn't their fault. Talking in an entertaining way is really, really,  really hard. That's why this piece exists. Rising Tide is designed to make anyone look good! This piece comes in 2 speeds.
credit: "Rising Tide" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rising Tide (faster)
description: Let's be fair, if your interview segment was already energetic, you  don't need something like this to fix it. Most people suck at interviews. It isn't their fault. Talking in an entertaining way is really, really,  really hard. That's why this piece exists. Rising Tide is designed to make anyone look good! This piece comes in 2 speeds.
credit: "Rising Tide (faster)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rite of Passage
description: Nice laid-back tribal all percussion piece with overtones of polynesian music.
credit: "Rite of Passage" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rites
description: Heavy and deep, the chords of this piece resemble Gregorian Chanting with resounding reverb as a harp plucks a few solitary notes. The music evokes an ancient ritual or ceremony, but could also be used for a tragic medieval funeral.
credit: "Rites" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ritual
description: Very very slow piece featuring the alto flute.
credit: "Ritual" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: River Fire
description: This piece has 54 beats each minute. At Angkor Wat, a Hindu temple carving has 54 gods in opposition to 54 demons, and in their struggle they create immortality. Mystics (or mathematicians... whatever) in Ancient Greece knew of the prime factorization of this mystic number. 3 by 3 by 3 by 2. What does this all mean? Not much, as it turns out the concept of a "minute" wasn't familiar to the architects at Angkor Wat.
credit: "River Fire" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: River Flute
description: I enjoy relaxing background music things. I looked out into the world for this music, and there was a lot of music, but none of it was right. When I want calm - this is the kind of thing I want! Super crazy hit-you-in-the-head calm! I want mega-aggro-calm. The flute in this recording is a standard C flute slowed to half speed. The river is running at normal river speed.
credit: "River Flute" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: River of Io
description: I would like to state, for the record, that this is the worst river cruise I've ever taken. The zombie crocodiles were bad enough, but the chase for the stolen artifact statue that was taken by the Ice Monkey Lord was really quite too much. And now I'm missing my left shoe. So why are we up sneaking around UFO landing sites? NONE OF THIS MAKES ANY SENSE!!! You got some clandestine stuff going on? This track will probably work for any sneakiness anywhere.
credit: "River of Io" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: River Valley Breakdown
description: Bluegrass country music.
credit: "River Valley Breakdown" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Road to Hell
description: A slow dark piece featuring a piano, bass duet.  Begins with bass, then immediately piano comes in.  Piece has continuous bass with piano coming in and out.  Finishes with prolonged bass note.
credit: "Road to Hell" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Robo-Western
description: A smooth glitchy action piece with a guitar sound inspired by Morricone and a setting that is very contemporary.
credit: "Robo-Western" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Robobozo
description: Deeply satisfying synths play in a slightly dystopian domain. So if you have a film where a future vampire who owns a travelling carnival comes back in time to today with a crazy assemblage of experiences for today's currently not-yet-jaded audiences... that is your piece! Also useful for cat parkour.
credit: "Robobozo" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rock Hybrid
description: Very very clean rock/hip-hop hybrid with some trance elements. EQ'ed dark, vocals should cut right through. Loopable.
credit: "Rock Hybrid" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rock on Chicago
description: Wesley Willis inspired rock music. C major.
credit: "Rock on Chicago" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rock Over London
description: Wesley Willis inspired rock music. A minor.
credit: "Rock Over London" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rocket
description: Euro-tech with some highly processed guitar lines and symphonic elements.
credit: "Rocket" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rocket Power
description: Funky drum machines? Yes, please! Also a killer bass line. This is both big and fun... kind of like the Paul Bunyan Experience... if Paul Bunyan were hip. Unlike most of my tunes, this one has an actual ending! Uncompressed download comes with all the parts to make your own mixes - should this one be insufficient.
credit: "Rocket Power" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rollin at 5
description: Acoustic version of "Rolling at 5".
credit: "Rollin at 5" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rollin at 5 - electronic
description: Electronic only version of "Rolling at 5".
credit: "Rollin at 5 - electronic" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ropocolypse 2
description: With a name like "Ropocolypse", it is probably digital and gritty.
credit: "Ropocolypse 2" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Round Drums
description: A collection of mostly large drums. Useful for action scenes.
credit: "Round Drums" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Royal Banana
description: Comically voiced and constructed. Slower (at 90BPM) but it still moves along.
credit: "Royal Banana" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Royal Coupling
description: Light and airy, with a bit of a march going on. Parallel chords and Ravel-like crescendo.
credit: "Royal Coupling" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rumination
description: After everything is said and done and you have time to look back, this piece unfolds like one's mind coming to terms with situations of gravity.
credit: "Rumination" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Run Amok
description: Super comedy action sequence. You'll know if you need this.
credit: "Run Amok" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Rynos Theme
description: Starts small, gets big... then smaller, then REALLY big... then small again. Kind of like a turtle. Actually, it is entirely possible that I just kept seeing different turtles. I mean, they all sort of look like turtles; I wasn't tagging them or marking them with chalk or anything. Chalk will probably just wash off in the pond anyway. Oh! Kind of like a puffer fish! Like a musical puffer fish! Perfect.
credit: "Rynos Theme" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sad Trio
credit: "Sad Trio" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Salty Ditty
description: Avast ye maties! All your boat are belong to us! Super chipper piratey-like 8bit tune. I mean, it could be used for non-nautical things, but the audience will probably be all like "Hey! Why is there an 8-bit pirate shanty going on here!?" Perfectly loopable for all your casual seafaring games. Or game reviews. Or actual voyages. Or voyage reviews.
credit: "Salty Ditty" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Samba Isobel
description: Do you eat dinner with no amuse bouche? Then you are not classy enough for this high energy background masterpiece. It exceeds all classiness classifications. It can seem cheery, but that's really just more classiness. The slightly lazy bass player? Classy.
credit: "Samba Isobel" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Samba Stings
description: Various 2-4 second stings based on "Modern Jazz Samba".
credit: "Samba Stings" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sancho Panza gets a Latte
description: Acoustic guitar, latin percussion, bass, alto flute, trumpet, and... accordion. Sort of Spanish, sort of French.
credit: "Sancho Panza gets a Latte" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sapphire Isle
description: Arpeggiation and scales in an unusual chordal setting.
credit: "Sapphire Isle" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sardana
description: Intimate guitar dance piece, probably too rubato to be an actual Sardana, but it didn't sound enough like a Farruca to call it that. "Vaguely Spanish Guitar Music" also seemed wrong.
credit: "Sardana" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Satiate
description: I piece unlike anything I've done, this is a very difficult piece to process emotionally. It just never lets the audience rest. There are a lot of uses for this sort of piece.  It is also available with just the percussion, and just the strings... both of which are quite different from the combined.
credit: "Satiate" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Satiate - only percussion
description: Highly effected percussion piece at a mid tempo. This track was extracted from a larger work, but will lend some motion and reserved immediacy to any scene.
credit: "Satiate - only percussion" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Satiate - only strings
description: I piece unlike anything I've done, this is a very difficult piece to process emotionally. It just never lets the audience rest. There are a lot of uses for this sort of piece.  It is also available with percussion, which gives it a more immediacy.
credit: "Satiate - only strings" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sauropod Spotting
description: This piece is one of three pieces that was inspired by a trip to a dinosaur-themed roadside attraction that had "dinosaur music". That music was recorded in the early 1990s, and sounds a bit cheesy today, so I tried to update it. This piece is a hybrid of triggered samples and live recordings.
credit: "Sauropod Spotting" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Savannah (Sketch)
description: This is NOT a complete piece. It is only a sketch developed as a test for a stage production (repeated many times).  If you only need a few seconds, it is fine. Loping feel in 3/4 time.
credit: "Savannah (Sketch)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sax, Rock, and Roll
description: Lots of guitars with a sax-y hook.
credit: "Sax, Rock, and Roll" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Scattershot
description: Fast tempo and loose timing gives this piece some not-quite-in-control speed.
credit: "Scattershot" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Scheming Weasel (faster version)
description: Sort of cartoonish, and yet sort of dark. I couldn't decide the tempo, so I posted a slower and faster version of the piece.
credit: "Scheming Weasel (faster version)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Scheming Weasel (slower version)
description: Sort of cartoonish, and yet sort of dark. I couldn't decide the tempo, so I posted a slower and faster version of the piece.
credit: "Scheming Weasel (slower version)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Scissors
description: Subtle atmospheric sounds and rain-like cymbal elements blend together, creating an aura of intensity and intrigue, suitable for a mysterious or suspenseful production. The sounds build in force just before the end.
credit: "Scissors" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: SCP-x1x (Gateway to Hell)
description: Some nice soul-sucking horror music. It looks like an innocent birthday cake. Something mom might buy down at the Jewel’s. It showed up at the holiday party for our Class D personnel last year, but no one knows who brought it. It may be related to SCP-1117. Here’s the problem; you look at that cake too long and it looks back into you. First it fills you with dread, then it fills you with buttercream, ruining your pristine run of ketosis. You were just making progress! Dammit, Cake Demon!
credit: "SCP-x1x (Gateway to Hell)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: SCP-x2x (Unseen Presence)
description: Dark horror soundscape. There are places of evil in the world. Dark places. There are places that absorb life with their greasy tendrils of unlight. There are places that screw up everyone's sandwiches. There are places that delay postal packages. There are places that cause internet outages right when you're down to the last 4 players in an online 1 vs 100 Tetris tournament. There are places of evil in the world. Dark places.
credit: "SCP-x2x (Unseen Presence)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: SCP-x3x (I am Not OK)
description: Dark horror soundscape with technological and mechanical overtones.
credit: "SCP-x3x (I am Not OK)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: SCP-x4x (Mind Leech)
description: Grating Horror Soundscape. Welcome to the Open House! I’m Kathy, your realtor. You’ll probably want to keep your shoes on. On your left is the living room, complete with ornate working fireplace. It’s fueled by the souls of the damned AND it heats the whole house! Mind yourself around the walls, they can get a little grabby if they haven’t been fed yet. Up the stairs and to your right is piece de resistance... the jacuzzi tub! The water filtration system gets out most of the blood. Now, about the attic...
credit: "SCP-x4x (Mind Leech)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: SCP-x5x (Outer Thoughts)
description: Nice, but creepy music for storytelling. Simple melodies played on that old piano your grandma had in her basement. It was once great, but has since become a spider and dust motel. I'm sure the spiders think it is pretty great. Gotta be loud if you're a piano spider, but rent control totally makes it worth it.
credit: "SCP-x5x (Outer Thoughts)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: SCP-x6x (Hopes)
description: Haunting music for storytelling; With a cello. Cello, bassoon, and piano are known to be expert haunters. This piece has no bassoon, but 2 out of 3 does get pretty haunting!
credit: "SCP-x6x (Hopes)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: SCP-x7x (6th Floor)
description: Somewhat urgent music for storytelling. Winding staircase that leads to nowhere... like your liberal arts degree. Melodic enough to hold your interest. Repetitive enough for you to lose interest.
credit: "SCP-x7x (6th Floor)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Screen Saver
description: Blip bloop?  Bloopity BlooBlip! BlooBlip?! Blibbity blib blib blib! Blip bloop. Blippity bloop bloop BLOOP! :-)
credit: "Screen Saver" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Second Coming - no percussion
description: A loop-based piece, I've gotten a lot of requests for a version of this with no percussion or voice - so here you go. Broad and inspiring.
credit: "Second Coming - no percussion" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Secret of Tiki Island
description: Co-written with Bryan Teoh while he was on vacation (Thanks Bryan!) this is all the mystery and chill groove you need. So come on you cats and swingers, enjoy yourself a Jet Pilot (served in a pineapple of course) and help unravel the Secret of Tiki Island! Can you save yourself and the island from the Volcano!? No. Of course you can't. It is a freaking VOLCANO. If the pyroclastic flows and lahars don't kill you, the carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide probably will. Uncompressed download comes with 10 different stems so you can mix your own!
credit: "Secret of Tiki Island" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Secrets of the Schoolyard
description: Sort of dark and mysterious, while still being current-sounding and light. Got a mystery in the city? I got your music! Crazy deep bass in lots of parts… careful when mixing this one.
credit: "Secrets of the Schoolyard" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Semi-Funk
description: Horn Section with a couple of solos. Nice hook, and the upright bass is beautiful.
credit: "Semi-Funk" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Senbazuru
description: Beautiful warm and calming piece with a Japanese sort of sound. A low end synth provides deep support.
credit: "Senbazuru" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Send for the Horses
description: Floaty! Ethereal! Useful for dream sequences. Or those montages of sad people standing in the rain.
credit: "Send for the Horses" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Serene
description: A slow, very calm piece featuring English horn, piano, and bass. Center section also has brass ensemble and strings.
credit: "Serene" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sergio's Magic Dustbin
description: This piece starts very slow and builds... like Bolero. Unlike Bolero, this piece builds beyond the safety limit and gets crazy. I recommend you check out the piece from 1 minute 48 seconds in. There are several break points you can start from to get to the crazy payoff faster, or use the whole thing!
credit: "Sergio's Magic Dustbin" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Serpentine Trek
description: Something winding its way somewhere.
credit: "Serpentine Trek" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Seven March
description: A piece in 7/8 time with 2-measure phrasing. Very dark and round sounding with randomly placed percussions.
credit: "Seven March" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Seven Off
description: Lots of strings, a couple of winds carry the interest offset by a glockenspiel. 7-4 time. Slow and unnerving.
credit: "Seven Off" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Seventh Seal
description: Simple drone followed by a crescendo leading to silence.
credit: "Seventh Seal" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Severe Tire Damage
description: Ultra-cool downtempo piece with faster driving percussions. Want to look cool? Make this your theme song. Play it loud enough and you can use it for pro-wrestling entrance music! Uncompressed download comes with a bonus 96bpm set.
credit: "Severe Tire Damage" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shades of Spring
description: Sort of a minor mid-tempo jazz combo with 2 pianos. Melody is doubled in octaves. Soloist goes outside more than the guy comping... but hey - what are soloists for?
credit: "Shades of Spring" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shadowlands 1 - Horizon
description: Part one of seven. Sort of an edgy-underwater feel... which isn't common. You can feel the struggle just trying to get the sounds out. Imagine a small rhinoceros at a tea party. The image you have in your head has nothing to do with this piece; But it is quite amusing.
credit: "Shadowlands 1 - Horizon" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shadowlands 2 - Bridge
description: Part two of seven. Very close clusters of tones bring the tension! And that tension wanes and waxes without notice. If you want your audience to be concerned, this is how you do it.
credit: "Shadowlands 2 - Bridge" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shadowlands 3 - Machine
description: Part three of seven. Part pipe organ, part broken pipe organ, this isn't just spooky, it is crazy spooky. It also has a musical theme, which not all of this horror moody stuff has. Consider it the jelly filling in your horror doughnut.
credit: "Shadowlands 3 - Machine" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shadowlands 4 - Breath
description: Part four of seven. This is the pizza cutter of this series, round and edgy. It has a little bit of melodic complexity, but mostly it just sits around being creepy. Should work well under dialog.
credit: "Shadowlands 4 - Breath" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shadowlands 5 - Antechamber
description: Part five of seven. Airy, but not in the "I'm outdoors, and everything is great 'airy'" way. More like the "the alien machine that sustains our life is slowly breaking down and poison is beginning to seep from its core" way. Whatever is happening... it isn't fast, and it isn't good.
credit: "Shadowlands 5 - Antechamber" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shadowlands 6 - The Pit
description: Part alien cacophony, part organic awfulness, part six of seven. If you set this piece as music you wake up to in the morning, you're going to have a bad, bad day. There will be half remembered monsters from the times of not-asleep, not-awake... whose only jobs are to induce unexpected nausea inside government buildings.
credit: "Shadowlands 6 - The Pit" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shadowlands 7 - Codex
description: Part seven of seven. A real mind bender. This one is all acoustic, and no artificial synths, so it has an organic feel. Not Certified Organic, just normal organic. So, that means it looks better, requires less fertilizer, has fewer pests and a higher yield.
credit: "Shadowlands 7 - Codex" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shamanistic
description: Earthy, yet unearthly. Deep and rich with things amiss.
credit: "Shamanistic" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shaving Mirror
description: Hey, yo - welcome to the sic'est grammar podcast on the planet, where your future will have been perfectly continuous. I can't really think up much more in the realm of grammar jokes without going to the "dangling participle". And that's not happening.
credit: "Shaving Mirror" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sheep May Safely Graze - BWV 208
description: Bach. Abnormal instrumentation.
credit: "Sheep May Safely Graze - BWV 208" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shenyang
description: When I do music based on folk traditions, I tend to name them after cities. Like this one: Shenyang. It is a little village of 8 million people that I've somehow never heard of. Oh sure, I've heard the name, but I don't associate it with anything specific. Chicago: Hot Dogs. Amsterdam: Offensively tall Dutch. Moscow: "Stop a Douchebag". Shenyang: No clue. How did I miss this city?? You already know if you need this piece, it has a more satisfying low-end than actual real Chinese music, and it should fit in with your modern productions well.
credit: "Shenyang" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shiny Tech
description: Electronica (techo-pop dance). This is a fast and energetic piece polished almost to a fault. Lots of synth, and a happy clave. Think fashion show runway. Works best loud, works also not so loud.
credit: "Shiny Tech" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shiny Tech II
description: Electronica (techo-pop dance). Much like its predecessor, but with a brand new, less pop main synth line.
credit: "Shiny Tech II" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Shores of Avalon
description: Highly processed piano with lots of subtle synths and vocal effects. Grows in intensity after the 3 minute mark, then calms again.
credit: "Shores of Avalon" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Show Your Moves
description: Your toe will start tapping to the bump of the bass drum once the music pans through your speakers.  This song is one for a successful accomplishment or the happy ending to a difficult challenge.  The staccato melody resembles a synthesized tremolo violin, while the bass guitar thumps increase  in prominence until they are your heartbeat.
credit: "Show Your Moves" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Showdown
description: Starts unnerving; ends calming.
credit: "Showdown" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sidewalk Shade
description: Just a nice little jazz piece. A slower version is also available.
credit: "Sidewalk Shade" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sidewalk Shade - slower
description: Just a nice little jazz piece. A faster version is also available.
credit: "Sidewalk Shade - slower" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Silent Night
credit: "Silent Night" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Silly Fun
description: This is a set of 2 happy bubble-gummy themes for a comic platformer-type video game. Also included in the mp3 file are three different endings - quick, longer, and other.
credit: "Silly Fun" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Silver Blue Light
description: Sparse in it?s instrumentation, Silver Blue Light is quiet and pensive with atmospheric synthesized chords and guitar.. There isn?t much of a melodic line to this piece until well into the fifth minute. In the third minute the guitar plays a few high notes, and the key changes briefly, which occurs again in the final twenty seconds as well.
credit: "Silver Blue Light" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Silver Flame
description: Life is the source of mystical potential. Or it isn't. One of the two. If I had to bet... I would probably ask what those words mean. Even 'life' isn't simple. I don't think I could recognize what the first living thing was. It is like making a soup. Hot water? Not soup. Hot water with salt? Not soup. Add a potato? Still not soup. That's just a potato in hot salt water. At some point it becomes soup. Same with life. Bonus fact: Borscht was never soup. It is borscht.
credit: "Silver Flame" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Simple Duet
description: Slower, optimistic and simple duet.
credit: "Simple Duet" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Simple Music to Frighten Small Children By
description: If the title doesn't say it... The sound was accomplished by recording a piano, doubling the recording and pitching one down almost an octave while pitching the other up almost an octave.
credit: "Simple Music to Frighten Small Children By" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Simplex
description: Thin, dark, moody piece that accelerates to the end. Remarkably metered and free at the same time. Guitar is all half muted.
credit: "Simplex" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sincerely
description: Talk wistfully about the past.  Talk hopefully about the future.  Talk about your hopes and fears.  Talk about your neighborhood watch lady.  Talk about your chill tracks!
credit: "Sincerely" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sinfonia No. 3 in D Major - BWV 789
description: Bach's 3-part invention with a hip beat and bass. The notes are all Bach's, but are not all in the correct order.
credit: "Sinfonia No. 3 in D Major - BWV 789" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sinfonia Number 5
description: J. S. Bach's 3-part invention that I hacked together for music for a "stuffy aristocratic dinner party". Of all the Sinfonias, I think this works the best for that.
credit: "Sinfonia Number 5" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sing Along with Jim
description: Peppy yet easy children's music designed to be easy to make up a song to.
credit: "Sing Along with Jim" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Skye Cuillin
description: New age and Celtic with super round synths and lots of delay.
credit: "Skye Cuillin" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sleep and Then
description: Winds descending, strings ascending. Slow, nice.
credit: "Sleep and Then" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Slow Burn
description: Super nice progressive rock/blues piece with 3 sections.
credit: "Slow Burn" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Slow Heat
description: Very simple polyrhythms and polymelodies.
credit: "Slow Heat" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Slow Jam
description: Well, this is interesting... Smooth sine bass contrasted with a lovely excited drum machine and then... the magic! Genre bending magic! You're a cool kid right? This is for you. You're welcome. Think 'trap' meets 'R&B' meets 'shoegaze' meets some other genre that is SO COOL there isn't even a name for it yet. Download comes with a not-quite-so-slow version that is not quite so slow.
credit: "Slow Jam" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Slow Ska Game Loop
description: Two very different synths bracket the highs and lows of this piece. Loopable for things that require looping.
credit: "Slow Ska Game Loop" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Smash (Sketch)
description: This is NOT a complete piece. It is only a sketch developed as a test for a stage production (repeated many times).  If you only need a few seconds, it is fine. This piece has a harsh ting-y electric piano on top.
credit: "Smash (Sketch)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Smoking Gun
description: Gritty Western feel with a touch of suspense.
credit: "Smoking Gun" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Smooth Lovin
description: This one got turned up to 11. I started producing this as a parody... then I really started liking it, so I guess it is a pastiche now? Oh, man... I wish there was an allowance for pastiche in copyright like there is for parody.
credit: "Smooth Lovin" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Smooth Move
description: A Simple Bass Groove with High Hat and Snare behind it. The repeated bass line is good for dancing.
credit: "Smooth Move" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Smoother Move
description: Super rubato piano solo.
credit: "Smoother Move" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Snare Bounce Polka
description: Swing.
credit: "Snare Bounce Polka" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sneak 'n Get Caught
description: Low strings / glass harmonica. Wind/String/Percussion diminished chord build with crescendo and sting on the end. (written for Darker Projects' Falcon Banner Episode 4)
credit: "Sneak 'n Get Caught" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sneaky
description: Ascending and descending chromatic scales gives this piece an air of mischief; perfectly suited for a cartoon. It has moments of tenuous fluidity, rapid motion, and a touch of suspense, making it perfect for the classic scene where the hero is sneaking past the sleeping giant.
credit: "Sneaky" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sneaky Adventure
description: Tight pizz string section, joined by a lone bassoon on the recapitulation.
credit: "Sneaky Adventure" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sneaky Snitch
description: An oboe and a snare drum dance a tantalizing number with the whimsical plucks of a string quartet. The staccato nature of the music suggests walking on tiptoes, while the nasal notes of the oboe flits about almost imperceptibly. In the final minute, the string quartet plays a simple rhythm, before the oboe and snare drum crescendo to the finale.
credit: "Sneaky Snitch" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Soaring
description: While not an epic hour-long relaxation juggernaut, Soaring is an excellent relaxation workhorse with just enough mystical qualities to keep it from being truly peaceful.  Imagine a calm monkey hanging out at a remote monastery who, from time to time, will touch a tree - causing the tree to age a decade in a matter of seconds. I mean... still pretty calm, but something isn't right about that.
credit: "Soaring" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sock Hop
description: 1950's era simple rock with tremolo lead guitar and vibraphone. Almost surf music.
credit: "Sock Hop" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Some Amount of Evil
description: Starts at a fast pace, and slows.
credit: "Some Amount of Evil" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Somewhere Sunny
description: Simple, clean guitar duet.
credit: "Somewhere Sunny" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Somewhere Sunny (ver 2)
description: This is a longer version of the very popular "Somewhere Sunny". Simple, clean guitar duet.
credit: "Somewhere Sunny (ver 2)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Son of a Rocket
description: Deeply bassy club-style chords.
credit: "Son of a Rocket" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sonata 17
description: A short piece for small orchestra. The flutes play off the bassoon well. The B section includes a pleasant string theme. This piece culminates in a nice, easy ending.
credit: "Sonata 17" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Song of the Volga Boatmen
description: Yo, Heave Ho! The classic theme of difficult drudgery. Based on a Russian folk song.
credit: "Song of the Volga Boatmen" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Soporific
description: A laid-back chill, and chilling piece.
credit: "Soporific" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Southern Gothic
description:
Are you cool? Cool like a vampire planking in a graveyard in Alabama? 
Planking is uncool... so, you gotta be really, REALLY cool to pull off this vibe.
Stomp and clap along to the cooperating banjos!
credit: "Southern Gothic" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sovereign
description: Very very good new age piano solo in a minor. You might think 6 minutes is a bit long, but it isn't. Played on a darkly voiced piano. This piece should in no way be offered for free.
credit: "Sovereign" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sovereign Quarter
description: A re-recording of an older piece of mine on a new sample set of a Steinway Model D. This one is tuned to Quarter Comma Meantone (and not standard Equal Temperament).  In this piece, it gives an unerringly warm feel, as the notes that would be least in tune in this are never used.
credit: "Sovereign Quarter" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Space 1990
description: Do you have enough 1990's space music in your collection? Probably not. If you're unclear what 1990s pace music is, just take a listen. A slightly different mix is also available at a faster tempo.
credit: "Space 1990" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Space 1990-B
description: This is about as fast as you can reasonably push such a piece. Smooth and warm.
credit: "Space 1990-B" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Space Fighter Loop
description: Written as a background loop for a space fighting video game.
credit: "Space Fighter Loop" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Space Jazz
description: While working on a video game, the script called for "Space Jazz". I don't know if that is a thing, but this is what I made. Sounds like Space Jazz to me!
credit: "Space Jazz" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Space X-plorers
description: Background padding with an open wondrous feel.
credit: "Space X-plorers" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Spacial Harvest
description: Deep unsettling piece with no repeated themes. Fat, rounded bass drone with very high pitched interest on top.
credit: "Spacial Harvest" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Spacial Winds
description: Clear bowed-bell theme over a sweeping dark digital pad.
credit: "Spacial Winds" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Spazzmatica Polka
description: Boisterous and nearly obnoxious, this piece will lodge itself in your brain and make you think you?re trapped in an arcade. The polka rhythm is quick and the melody is spastic. Right into the second minute the rhythm drops out and introduces a crazed, comedic melody that continues throughout until the abrupt end.
credit: "Spazzmatica Polka" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Special Spotlight
description: So you're producing an interview segment! Problem is most people suck at being interviewed. Like... almost everyone. What do you do? You could send the non-media professional to an improv class, you could do 5 pre-interview coachings, or you could schedule a 3-day "pre-interview" at an all-inclusive beach resort in hopes that you will "share a moment" and uncover some goddamn humanity in your interview subject. Or. You could just put some interesting music behind the segment. If your crap interview is longer than this piece Do NOT loop this music - fire your editor.
credit: "Special Spotlight" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Spellbound
description: Reverbs, reverbs, reverbs! You want reverbs in you music, you got reverbs right here! Room reverbs, plate reverbs, even some spring reverbs! It is amazing! It is incredible! How can there be so much reverb?! So... why... You get a very hollow spooky thin feeling with the reverbs. This started out as an attempt to understand Witch House music. Pretty sure I still don't understand it.
credit: "Spellbound" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Spider Eyes
description: Spider Eyes is an eerie soundscape created with distant high strings, dissonant non-percussive piano textures, and alternately tuned bells.  This piece features much sustain and space.
credit: "Spider Eyes" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Spider's Web
description: Harpsichord in tritones with a bass pedal.
credit: "Spider's Web" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Spirit of the Girl
description: There are 54 beads on a Buddhist prayer mala. These are used for counting recitations and chants. There are 54 beats per minute in this song. Coincidence? Sure is. What, you're going through an entire mala cycle in a minute? That's crazy talk! Studies have shown the optimal number of mantras in a single set is somewhere between 15 and 20 anyway... so don't waste your money on the 54 or 108 bead versions. You'll be a lot better doing more sets of less reps. And don't forget leg day.
credit: "Spirit of the Girl" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Split In Synapse
description: A short piece that mixes the symphony with frenzied electronica elements and a dance beat. The horns are blasting and discordant, the synthesizer is manic, the effects disorienting, and the final cresecendo push is loud and forceful.
credit: "Split In Synapse" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Spring Thaw
description: Simple melody. Something feels amiss here, but in a sort of pleasing way
credit: "Spring Thaw" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Spy Glass
description: The year is... I have no idea. Timeless. Could be now, could be in the 1950s. Super cool jazz for your hardcore detectives! Also useful for beat poets! Also useful for ennui or boredom! Well, interesting sorts of boredom.
credit: "Spy Glass" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Spy Groove
description: Aggressive drum kit sound with warmth added by a B3 organ and conga. Modulation in the final repeat.
credit: "Spy Groove" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Stages of Grief
description: That sort of "I'm kind of 'ok', but I'm still standing out in the rain feel". Pretty depressing for being in a major key.
credit: "Stages of Grief" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Starry
description: C major with a minor IV chord.
credit: "Starry" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Starting Out Waltz Allegretto
description: This is more for practicing dance than anything else. It never changes, it never gets interesting. This is important if you don't want to trip over your feet while drilling a dance step.
credit: "Starting Out Waltz Allegretto" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Static Motion

credit: "Static Motion" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Stay the Course
description: A low rumble marks the seconds. Out of nowhere comes nothing! Just a continuous ominous force, never seen. You can see the ominous force if you sprinkle some iron filing around.
credit: "Stay the Course" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Stealth Groover
description: The constancy of the bass melts into your consciousness, as the syncopation of the high-pitched piano and electric guitar keep the groove flowing. Subtle synthesizer arrangements change the flow of the song and keep it interesting, while the rhythm section is playful and experimental. This is perfect for a scene where the spy learns a new skill or performs an act of guile, or as the background to a low-key, tech-oriented game.
credit: "Stealth Groover" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Steel and Seething
description: Nice build-up and release. See also: Medusa
credit: "Steel and Seething" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Steel Rods

description: Good old fashioned pickin and stompin!
credit: "Still Pickin" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

credit: "StompDance" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Stoneworld Battle

title: Stormfront

credit: "Stormfront" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Street Party
description: This is my impression of a tv show street party scene scored by a composer from the 90s. #TexasSharpshooterFallacy
credit: "Street Party" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Strength of the Titans
description: Oh, this is a big one. Short, but big. There's nothing wrong with either of those things.
credit: "Strength of the Titans" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: String Impromptu Number 1
description: Soaring and delicate piece for full string orchestra.
credit: "String Impromptu Number 1" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Study And Relax
description: Like a worn out record with a mis-punched spindle hole. Thanks, izope! :-)
credit: "Study And Relax" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
