description: Cool, cool funk. Some horns for punctuation.
credit: "Style Funk" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Suave Standpipe
description: You know what's cool? A standpipe in the winter. I imagine this one with a hip mustache and a plaid beret. Enough of the imagery, this is a little downtempo chill piece with lush horn punctuation. Suitable for: walks in the rain, time-lapse videos, sad cooking shows.
credit: "Suave Standpipe" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sugar Plum Breakdown
description: Just the final part of Tchaikovsky's piece with giant percussion and synths.
credit: "Sugar Plum Breakdown" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sugar Plum Dark Mix
description: Tchaikovsky's dance  from the Nutcracker with lots of percussion and extra choirs.
credit: "Sugar Plum Dark Mix" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Summer Day
description: Soothing piece with an interesting harmonic left-turn. You got a savage beast? This is just the ticket.
credit: "Summer Day" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Summon the Rawk
description: Double kick drums, aggressive bass... perfect for: entrance music for pro-wrestlers, annoying the neighbors, playing "air drums", long walks on the beach.
credit: "Summon the Rawk" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sunday Dub
description: This was written for a sneaky-yet-cool scene. The kind where our main character is trailing a subject to find out where they get the amazing cheese they serve at their restaurant. There's a bunch of bits where the paranoid restauranteur turns around unexpectedly and Private Detective Alice Winterbottom has to duck behind dumpsters, or spin around casually pretending to be on a phone call, or hide behind a watermelon at the fruit stand.
credit: "Sunday Dub" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sunflower Dance Party
description: As much fun as you can have with a cowbell! Lots and lots of cowbell.  I wrote this one when I was particularly depressed, and it fixed it. I didn't want it to end, so I kept modulating it; that's why it is longer than most.
credit: "Sunflower Dance Party" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sunset at Glengorm
description: Processed piano is featured, leaving a deep uncertain texture. Tempo is highly variable.
credit: "Sunset at Glengorm" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sunshine
description: A bright piece with piano and rhythm guitar throughout.  Kit and Bass in the background.  Main melody carried by Piano.
credit: "Sunshine" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sunshine (version 2)
description: Slightly longer, slightly slower version of "Sunshine"
credit: "Sunshine (version 2)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Suonatore di Liuto
description: Simple little background lute piece.
credit: "Suonatore di Liuto" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Super Circus
description: Circus-type march.
credit: "Super Circus" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Super Friendly
description: Starts easy, builds, and releases easy again. Sort of like a happy triumph. Eucatastrophe, even.
credit: "Super Friendly" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Super Polka
description: Super smashing trumpets, and a crazy clarinet! Also guitars and such. Not your oom-pah kind of polka. This is all-out dance.
credit: "Super Polka" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Super Power Cool Dude
description: This piece was built almost entirely with arpeggiators. What does that mean for you? Probably nothing. But holy man! Does this sound like it is from 1983! So, pop a tape of "Flashdance" in your VCR... and then spend like 8 minutes rewinding it... because, apparently your cousin couldn't be bothered to do that. Seriously, Sally! You did the same thing when I lent you "Smokey and the Bandit II", and I didn't say anything because you had a hard week, but still managed to make the Jell-o Salad with the grapes for the family reunion... which was nice. Anyway, I'll probably just get you one of those $20 tape rewinders they have at Radio Shack for your birthday. I also enrolled you in the Battery of the Month Club. You're welcome.
credit: "Super Power Cool Dude" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Supernatural
description: A quick little piece to bring out supernatural elements.
credit: "Supernatural" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Supernatural Radio A
description: If you're looking for that late 40s/early 50s sci-fi or supernatural radio drama - this is your piece. This was rendered on a hammond, using only the drawbars that would make it over the radio (no bass).
credit: "Supernatural Radio A" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Surf Inspector
description: Bouncy piece, usable in spy setting.  Stays similar throughout, easily looped, if necessary.
credit: "Surf Inspector" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Surf Shimmy
description: I gotta admit, I've never been to a clambake, only ever fish boils... which are similar, except for clambakes usually involve mollusks and giant sea-bugs, and fish boils involve fish. Also, clambakes are more steaming and fish boils are more boiling. You're more likely to see Green Bay Packers jerseys at fish boils, and more likely to see New England Patriots jerseys at clambakes. This music is west-coast, though... The more I think about it - the less useful this descriptive paragraph becomes. Uncompressed download comes with a couple mild variations, including "Psychedelic".
credit: "Surf Shimmy" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Suvaco do Cristo
description: Named for a region in Rio, this Brazilian-style carnival piece has a deep dark thickness to it.
credit: "Suvaco do Cristo" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Sweeter Vermouth
description: The jaunty bass line keeps this short piece moving at a solid pace, while the vibraphone and saxophones play the swinging melody, until the bright, thump of an ending. Use this piece as a slick transition between scenes or for the background to a short scene of drinking, gambling, or dancing.
credit: "Sweeter Vermouth" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Swimmey Texture
description: Highly processed piano and synths that provide a deep, contemplative texture.
credit: "Swimmey Texture" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Symbiosis
description: Quiet solo piano in 3 parts with additional percussion bit adding in more and more to the end. My normal "feels" that are used to classify pieces are largely inadequate for this piece, as are the genres. In other words... I have no idea what this is.
credit: "Symbiosis" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Symmetry
description: This piece has a good beat and you can dance to it... assuming you are a dark, lurking horror with a betentacled face and an urge to consume life forces.
credit: "Symmetry" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tabuk
description: An epic plodding middle-eastern sounding piece. Grab your camels!
credit: "Tabuk" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tafi Maradi
description: Percussion beats and shakers instantly make your feet tap, involving you in the tribal experience of ritual kinship. Three sets of call-and-response chanting slide into the forefront of the beat, interspersed with rapid djembe solos to the ending when the dust finally settles.
credit: "Tafi Maradi" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tafi Maradi no voice
description: Percussion beats and shakers instantly make your feet tap, involving you in the tribal experience of ritual kinship. Three sets of call-and-response chanting slide into the forefront of the beat, interspersed with rapid djembe solos to the ending when the dust finally settles.
credit: "Tafi Maradi no voice" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Take a Chance
description: An out of control epic ride of adventure!
credit: "Take a Chance" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Take Me Out to the Ballgame
description: Ballpark organ playing the peppy classic.
credit: "Take Me Out to the Ballgame" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Take the Lead
description: This is a rough and hard-hitting piece, best used as background music to a stressful, strained scene, or tense and suspenseful content. Heavy distorted guitars begin the song, and at 0:41 the soaring synth leads play the melody while the powerful drums kick in.  A high-pitched pulsating synth effect carries the last seventeen seconds to the final punch.
credit: "Take the Lead" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Takeover of the 8-bit Synths
description: This... uhh... hmm... let's call it 'experimental' piece starts out with vanilla guitar and rock drums, and gets progressively crazier as the 8-bit synths take over the piece. Maximum anarchy starts around the 3-minute point.
credit: "Takeover of the 8-bit Synths" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tango de Manzana
description: A tango in 2 chords.
credit: "Tango de Manzana" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Taps v2
description: Solo trumpet version of the 1862 military ceremonial piece.
credit: "Taps v2" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tea Roots
description: Almost straight-up reggae, but with a chinese folk violin in it.
credit: "Tea Roots" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tech Live
description: Interview-Mania! This piece does nothing and goes nowhere. Perfect for an energetic backdrop to your review or interview segments!
credit: "Tech Live" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tectonic
description: Sister piece to Earth Prelude. Battle sequence.
credit: "Tectonic" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Teddy Bear Waltz
description: Technically speaking, I think this one is in 6/8 time... in which case, the tempo it 75. If it was notated in 3/4 time, the tempo would be 225 bpm. This piece took almost exactly one year to go from initial idea to produced piece. What was I doing for a whole year!? I mean... it doesn't exactly sound that difficult.
credit: "Teddy Bear Waltz" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Teller of the Tales
description: Simple subtle plucked duet of ancient-inspired origins.
credit: "Teller of the Tales" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Temple of the Manes
description: An ancient-feeling modal piece.
credit: "Temple of the Manes" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tempting Secrets
description: Starts with a big hit, and then a steady string drone with a beautiful flute line on top. Choirs kick in 2/3 of the way to bring up the mood.
credit: "Tempting Secrets" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Act One
description: This peculiar piece does have a story. If anyone would like to animate it, you'll have to bring your own script. Moderately large changes every minute or so. Accelerando at the end.
credit: "Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Act One" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Act Three
description: Metallic and generally unpleasant... yet I like this piece quite a bit. It gives the impression of a giant mechanical automaton.
credit: "Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Act Three" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Act Two
description: A fast deep unyielding sort of waltz-like-thing.
credit: "Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Act Two" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Intermission
description: Grooves for a bit, then changes up pretty hard with giant percussion.
credit: "Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Intermission" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Mermaid
description: Is she a mer-maid, or is she an illusion! Her enchanting voice will entice, and she is 100% alive! Keep your wits about you, gentlemen - you don't want to be dragged to an unfortunate end.  Very heavy on bass.
credit: "Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Mermaid" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Prelude
description: Originally released in a special collection as "Delayed Due to Dissonance", this piece is not part of a larger arc.
credit: "Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Prelude" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Snake Lady
description: One of the more sultry sideshow acts in the Tenebrous Brothers Carnival, The Snake Lady is a crowd favorite that most never forget, even if they don't remember exactly what happened during the show.
credit: "Tenebrous Brothers Carnival - Snake Lady" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Texture for Violincello and Pianoforte No. 2
description: An interesting jumble of cello and some piano fused together to create an eerie and intense piece the likes of which no one has ever heard of...until now.
credit: "Texture for Violincello and Pianoforte No. 2" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: That's a Wrap
description: Sparse music compatible for voice-over. This piece is related to the Rock piece "Welcome to the Show"
credit: "That's a Wrap" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: That Zen Moment
description: I picked up a round metal tongue drum from a local music store a while back, and thought the chords were beautiful. End of story! Enjoy the zen. :-)
credit: "That Zen Moment" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Thatched Villagers
description: Solid in pace, The Thatched Roof Villagers moves with percussion and a number of flutes and pipes struggling for dominance. The real joy of the piece is halfway through when the tinny dulcimer plays the melody and is then joined by the flutes in melody and harmony. The music is jovial and inviting. Loopable.
credit: "Thatched Villagers" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Thaxted (Holst)
description: Written by Gustav Holst, 1921; Arranged by Kevin MacLeod 2006. Originally published in a hymnbook - this piece took readily to the WWII retrospective type of arrangement.
credit: "Thaxted (Holst)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Bandit
description: Short Theme in two tempos for your bad guy.
credit: "The Bandit" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Britons
description: Tavern music like from the olden days.
credit: "The Britons" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Builder
description: Comedic, free-wheeling fun!
credit: "The Builder" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Cannery
description: A giant rousing mechanized heavy piano and heavy percussion piece, mildly reminiscent of Gershiwn or Scott - in 2 small sections.
credit: "The Cannery" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Chamber
description: Delicate start with a lush ending.
credit: "The Chamber" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Chase
description: Light and fast. For... well - chase sequences.
credit: "The Chase" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Complex
description: Mechanistic, electronic and organic. This piece gets very big around 1:46. (The preview is more 'boomy' than the download.)
credit: "The Complex" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Curtain Rises
description: A short bit of fanfare, like the kind that opens movies. Trillerific!
credit: "The Curtain Rises" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Descent
description: Driving piece without an overpowering melody. Should fit nicely into a lot of scenes.
credit: "The Descent" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Dread
description: Background horror music. Electronic. Slow, rumbly, and whiny Moderately unnerving.
credit: "The Dread" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Entertainer
description: Scott Joplin composition.
credit: "The Entertainer" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Escalation
description: One really long build. Generally gets faster, fuller and more exciting. Like "Bolero" but for suspense.
credit: "The Escalation" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Forest and the Trees
description: A peaceful exploration of the interplay between woodwinds weaving through a melody, underscored by soft brass chords. The music evokes scenes of nature, acceptance, and quietude.
credit: "The Forest and the Trees" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Hive
description: Cymbals and synthesizers evoke swarming insects, as whirring and clicking noises abound with heavy reverb.
credit: "The Hive" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The House of Leaves
description: A simple harp refrain plays a child?s melody, but is torn apart by discordant screeching noises, thumps, growls, and mechanical noises.
credit: "The House of Leaves" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Ice Giants
credit: "The Ice Giants" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Lift
description: A little trance-y and a dance-y, this piece takes a while to develop (like most EDM things these days). The full width of the piece is realized around 1:40. Not so much a drop and a gentle trip down a hill, really - but still satisfying! That note at the end? Surprisingly difficult to do that... I know you're thinking - Hey! That just sounds like noise! Well, yes and no. But it is worth it!
credit: "The Lift" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Machine Thinks
description: 100% electronic creepiness. Change from round and bleeping to harsh bleeping about 2 minutes in.
credit: "The Machine Thinks" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The North
description: Loopable small composition reminiscent of North American traditional music.
credit: "The North" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Other Side of the Door
description: A quick and off-color melody on the harp transports you to a mystical eerie world, while a flute plays a sweet melody, and pizzicato strings create a playful undertone. Quite a bit happens in this piece musically, it can be used to complement scenes of mischief, an eerie scene, or a world of magic and intrigue.
credit: "The Other Side of the Door" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Parting
description: I wrote this one December 27th, 2009 mainly for fun. It is a sweeping quiet piece until the past bit where is opens up a bit.  At 2:06, there is an oddly supported line with a 2+ octave gap between the melody and the supporting bass. At 2:28, the gap is filled triumphantly... It ends with a hollow dominant in 5 octaves, followed by a lush resolution.
credit: "The Parting" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Path of the Goblin King
description: This is sort of "Spooky Light". It is dark yet playful in a sense. Good for fairy tales or light tension building. It has several small arcs in it - but loops back to the begging.
credit: "The Path of the Goblin King" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Path of the Goblin King v2
description: Slightly faster version of the other similarly named piece, this one has an extra sense of urgency, but still retains the mystery and wonder bits.
credit: "The Path of the Goblin King v2" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Pyre
description: Vaguely medieval overtones. The opening section repeats in the second half with violins added.
credit: "The Pyre" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Reveal
description: Starts with cellos, adds horn, clarinet, English horn, contra-tuba - to a final sustained chord. Slow. Thin yet satisfying.
credit: "The Reveal" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Rule
description: I sort of regal opening brass fanfare. It is meant to join at the end with another piece of music... which has not been written yet. This works as a stand-alone opening for most anything.
credit: "The Rule" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Second Coming
description: A sound track piece with Kit and Trombones/French Horns throughout.  This piece includes sections from a public domain (librivox) reading of "The Second Coming."
credit: "The Second Coming" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Second Coming Instrumental
description: A sound track piece with Kit and Trombones/French Horns throughout.
credit: "The Second Coming Instrumental" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Show Must Be Go
description: Sort of inspired by the 1930s, and sort of inspired by all-out weird. Definitely recommend taking a listen to this piece. Make sure you get to the 1 minute mark... fun times trumpet playing await! I personally enjoy how the clarinet play tries to follow the trumpet player - doesn't work out so well.
credit: "The Show Must Be Go" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Sky of our Ancestors
description: We reflect, we dream, we are born. We gather together, we smile, we eat potato salads. We remember, we invent, muddle mint for our mojitos. We greet, we listen, we appreciate NetFlix. We collect coins and stamps... for some reason. We mix up the names of our children with the names of our pets. We x-ray baggage... with X-RAYS! Those things are like 200keV! Each! Do you know what that does to people!? Hint: Not good things.
credit: "The Sky of our Ancestors" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Small
description: Simple polyrhythms in a very small piece. Get it? Small!? Epsilon!?? Yeah... no worries. The fifth of a series.
credit: "The Small" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Snow Queen
description: Sort of exciting and sort of spooky in that fairy tale sort of way. This is one of my favorite pieces of late. Good interplay of instruments. You can listen to this one over and over. Handy, because it does loop back to the beginning. Major build starting at 1:50 or so.
credit: "The Snow Queen" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Voices
description: Almost comforting pad, were it not for the inhuman voice-like punctuations.
credit: "The Voices" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Way Out
description: Understated intensity with a hair of creepiness.
credit: "The Way Out" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Whip
description: The shorter theme written for the opening of The Whip Podcast. Starts off quick with a short drum roll, then continues with guitar.  Guitar used throughout, ends with a fade out using Kit.  Bass in the background only.
credit: "The Whip" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: The Whip (Extended Version)
description: The extended version of the show theme written for The Whip Podcast.  Aggressive, hip, theme.  Slow fade out at the end.  This version can be looped easier than the shorter version.
credit: "The Whip (Extended Version)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Theme for Harold (var. 1)
description: Simple simple 8-bit theme. This is the laziest and slowest of the three. It was originally written by a puppet, so mostly black keys, which are easier for a puppet to play.
credit: "Theme for Harold (var. 1)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Theme for Harold (var. 2)
description: Simple simple 8-bit theme. This is the mid-tempo version of the three. It was originally written by a puppet, so mostly black keys, which are easier for a puppet to play.
credit: "Theme for Harold (var. 2)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Theme for Harold (var. 3)
description: Simple simple 8-bit theme. This is the fastest "Boss Level" version of the three. It was originally written by a puppet, so mostly black keys, which are easier for a puppet to play.
credit: "Theme for Harold (var. 3)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: There is Romance
description: Slow and poignant, this piece is excellent for depicting childhood love, the swelling love of adolescence, or the tender caresses of old age. The simple, elegant melody is exceptionally suitable to weddings, faith services, or as a theme to a story of lasting love.
credit: "There is Romance" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: There It Is
description: Very quick and jovial, this brass heavy piece has a guitar riff that sticks in the brain, but ends suddenly. Useful for a quick theme introduction, transition, or for a fast and exciting commercial.
credit: "There It Is" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Thief in the Night
description: Laid-back, grooving, and cool. Did I mention cool? You need a cool piece. That is a statement you NEED a cool piece. Lucky for you, this IS a cool piece. Super clean production will allow this piece to fit into most things. I'd personally use this piece for a super badass character.
credit: "Thief in the Night" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Thinking Music
description: Comedic "hard thinking" music. Chances are you won't need the entire piece if you are making a film. I made it so you can cut it up into different sounding sections of various seriousness. If you're using it for a video game, everything flows together well, or you could loop sections that work best.
credit: "Thinking Music" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Thinking of You
description: Nice piece for a narrative voice-over of good times past, present or future.
credit: "Thinking of You" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Thinking Out Loud
description: Piano looped digital electronica hybrid. I started this piece in 2
credit: "Thinking Out Loud" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: This House
description: Delightfully creepy, this piece is really difficult to listen to without squirming a bit. I blame the violins... as we all should. Perfect for any scene where something just ain't right!
credit: "This House" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Thunder Dreams
description: This is more of a chordal soundscape than a drone. There is a little bit of hope here and there, but it is tempered with a deep sadness. Probably useful after a loss. Beautiful, horrible.
credit: "Thunder Dreams" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Thunderbird
description: Wikipedia describes the Thunderbird as "a supernatural bird of power and strength". It will also ask you to disambiguate it from the automobile made by Ford from 1955 to 2005. I'm sure it was a nice car. I've never owned one. But there were a lot of them! The late 70's Thunderbirds are particularly horrifying... They had those headlight covers that flipped up... because that was a good idea at some point. But this piece! Oh! This piece! Atmosphere like you wouldn't believe! The flute is just so earthy! The organic drones are also beautiful. The whole thing is beautiful. Kind of like you went to an alien day spa in another dimension where days last for years, but you still never get all wrinkly when you're in the bubbly warm waters. mmmm... bubbly warm waters... with the slight possibility of a serial killer.
credit: "Thunderbird" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Thunderhead
description: Native American drumming. The branch rattle is reminiscent of thunder. Tempo picks up about halfway through.
credit: "Thunderhead" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tiki Bar Mixer
description: How to make Tiki Drinks: Add rum. Add fruit juice. Add other rum. Add different fruit juice. Add another rum. Add some other juice thing. Top with crushed ice. Garnish with umbrella, flowers, pineapple, watermelon, small plastic dinosaurs, and sugar cane. Light on fire.
credit: "Tiki Bar Mixer" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tikopia
description: The feel of this percussion pieces switches from straight to swing several times, but always has a round wooden sound to it.
credit: "Tikopia" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Time Passes
description: Bittersweet and somewhat dark; ends brightly on an open major chord.
credit: "Time Passes" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tiny Fugue
description: A very short fugal theme. (3-part imitative counterpoint)
credit: "Tiny Fugue" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: To the Ends
description: Horns used in the background.  Main melodies carried by clarinet and strings.  Starts off bright, ends darker.
credit: "To the Ends" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Toccata and Fugue in D Minor
description: J. S. Bach's most famous organ piece. BWV 565. (Beckerath German baroque pipe organ)
credit: "Toccata and Fugue in D Minor" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Too Cool
description: You know when you watch a vampire movie and then you walk out into the real world, but you're still sort of in the fictional world because it looked like the real world... and that's where you are now. I call this Persistence of Fiction, and it feels awesome! Capture some fiction by playing this track while walking to the bus... er the Vampire Bus! or waiting in line at the Vampire DMV or sorting Vampire Direct Mail Ads or doing some Vampire Macrame.
credit: "Too Cool" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Touching Moments Five - Circle
description: A simple tour through every major key in order. Arpeggiated with some connecting melodic notes.
credit: "Touching Moments Five - Circle" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Touching Moments Four - Melody
description: More melodic than most of the pieces presented here - can be distracting, or can be just what you're looking for. Famous from the Sad Fairy Dress-up game.
credit: "Touching Moments Four - Melody" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Touching Moments One - Pulse
description: Open and airy. A classic "touching moment" style. Performance imperfections are exaggerated to give a more "choked up" feel.
credit: "Touching Moments One - Pulse" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Touching Moments Three - Deeper
description: A more 'gutsy' piece that explores more of the keyboard, and provides a more grounded and open feel.
credit: "Touching Moments Three - Deeper" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Touching Moments Two - Higher
description: Only notes from the very highest registers of the piano are used in this. It can cut through ambient noise and still provide a presence.
credit: "Touching Moments Two - Higher" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Touching Story
description: Very very slow and changeable.
credit: "Touching Story" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Townie Loop
description: Welcome to the town! If you have anything to sell, just put it in the box. The general store sells seeds. There is a Mountain Totem in the mountains. You can have a drink at the Iridium Bar. I need to tend to my giant melons now. That is not a euphemism. Bye!
credit: "Townie Loop" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tranquility
description: A calming meditative piece rendered on 4 iPhones using the Balls, Bloom, Bebot, and Ocarina applications.
credit: "Tranquility" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tranquility Base
description: Super chill, meditative, and massively long drone. The preview is cut to three minutes, but the entire download is 18 minutes, and more than 42 meg. Please be patient.
credit: "Tranquility Base" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Transition One
description: Small calm transition; descending wind ensemble blending to ascending string ensemble.
credit: "Transition One" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Trepidation
description: Background horror music. Solo piano; low and loud.
credit: "Trepidation" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Trio for Piano, Cello, and Clarinet
description: More contemplative than outright depressing. Tempo is highly variable, so don't count on it if you have to synch to something. I didn't know there was a tradition of writing for this instrumentation. It works very well.
credit: "Trio for Piano, Cello, and Clarinet" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Trio for Piano Violin and Viola
description: An unfinished trio in 2 main parts.
credit: "Trio for Piano Violin and Viola" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Trips It
description: A driving electronic piece.  Kit is dominant throughout the piece.  Choir has brief moments about 55 secs in, and re-emerging for a heavier role towards the end half of the piece.
credit: "Trips It" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Trouble
description: Diminished chords, tremolo You'll recognize them.
credit: "Trouble" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Trouble with Tribals
description: Another exciting guerrilla warfare planning meeting, and Parker didn't bring the coffee. I'm starting to get annoyed with Parker more and more these days. Sure, the new "cape cod style" curtains look great in the mud blinds, but I'm not into the satin obelisk in the middle of our jungle huts.
credit: "Trouble with Tribals" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Truth in the Stones
description: New age music. You know what is cool about New Age music? Low ambitions. It wants to do a simple thing, and then does it. No crazy counterpoint. No complicated harmonic structures. Just a simple simple thing. Like if Tetris was all those long blocks. Man, that would be great.
credit: "Truth in the Stones" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Truth of the Legend
description: Solo voice along with a small choir and giant percussion section. Ends in a sort of ethereal mode.
credit: "Truth of the Legend" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Twisted
description: A modern take on a 1970’s rock style.
credit: "Twisted" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Twisting
description: Let's talk about why so much film music sounds like this. The construction allows any part to be muted and otherwise sculpted around the dialog without the loss of a theme or motive energy. There isn't really a theme to lose. You can't hum this one easily. There is a lot of variation, but it is all in a very well defined range, and doesn't get too crazy.
credit: "Twisting" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Two Finger Johnny
description: Remember the old Casio and Yamaha "auto accompaniment" keyboards? This is a super-simple and freakishly-delightful terrible piece of music.
credit: "Two Finger Johnny" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Two Together
description: Sparkly open voicings.
credit: "Two Together" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Tyrant
description: Crank it up, ladies and gentlemen!  Come on! Let's go! You know HOW TO CRANK! Let's go clockwise! Like... clockwise from the top - not the bottom. Grab it from the top. Either hand. It doesn't matter. Now CRANK IT! Crank it. ...like how a clock moves. The other way. If you take the part farthest from  you and move it to the right... Counter-widdershins? You know what, it doesn't really need to be cranked.
credit: "Tyrant" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ujangong Mix
description: An epic clash of genre that feigns coherence. Based on the Public Domain 1904 recording of "Ujangong (Mask Dance)" from New Guinea. But with a swing bass and slicing techno chunk in 3/4 time.
credit: "Ujangong Mix" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ultra Polka
description: I tried to do an EDM piece using one of my new accordions... turns out, accordion just doesn't have the fast attack needed to do fast electronic things. The melody and chords were written for a diatonic button box, but I was never able to get the live recording to work. No worries! I just turned this monster up to 11. The uncompressed download comes with a faster and slower version.
credit: "Ultra Polka" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Ultralounge
description: You hip? You really hip? Oh, yeah you are! This piece comes from the coolest hippest parts of solar system... from a 1960s pad on the moon. Oh yeah. Dig it, man... dig it. The uncompressed download also comes with an even more chill mix.
credit: "Ultralounge" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Umbrella Pants
description: If naming tracks is so easy, you try it! Possibly sneaking, possibly comedic dialog, possibly comedic dialog while sneaking... 1,
credit: "Umbrella Pants" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Unanswered Questions
description: The solid beat and dark melody reverberate, giving the simplicity of this single-instrument piece the feeling of mounting tension and unease. Useful for a documentary showing pain, poverty, or imprisonment.
credit: "Unanswered Questions" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Undaunted
description: Big big drums pushing a big cinematic feel.
credit: "Undaunted" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Unease
description: Background horror music. Solo midrange piano.
credit: "Unease" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Unholy Knight
description: Oh geez, there's lots of notes in this one. The end of this piece is just woodwinds by themselves, and they are super cool. So often the percussion just takes over these pieces, even though there are some beautiful parts that get attention directed away from them.
credit: "Unholy Knight" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Unity
description: Big driving piano and drums piece for action goodness!
credit: "Unity" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Universal
description: Floating and grounding, this piece has a lot of bass guts but still a lot of reach on the high end. Perfect for retrospectives, automobile time lapses, drunken frat parties (black and white), and studying montages.
credit: "Universal" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Unlight
description: This piece is actively painful. It is ugly and nasty and dirty - about as much as you can be using exactly one orchestra. Seriously, there are occasional bits where there are notes - but mostly, it is just... uhh...
credit: "Unlight" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Unnatural Situation
description: Piano with a tape delay and lots of dark colour in the background.
credit: "Unnatural Situation" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Unpromised
description: Thin piece with surprising chordal structures in the second A section.
credit: "Unpromised" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Unseen Horrors
description: I originally wrote this as a piece for theramin, but I think it works better without.
credit: "Unseen Horrors" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Unwritten Return
description: Dreamy and edgy; Not a combination you often find, and yet - here it is. The ambiguous and slippery nature of the piece are a wonderful thing. Perfect for scoring a character where the audience is unsure of them. Could be good? Could be evil? WE DON'T KNOW!
credit: "Unwritten Return" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Up on a Housetop
description: Super-bouncy holiday sing-along.
credit: "Up on a Housetop" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Upbeat Forever
description: Ska! Ska! Ska! At least, I hope it gives that impression. Works pretty well for a lively background to most anything! This was written for an improv comedy group... so they would have something reasonable to sing to - if an audience member suggests it.
credit: "Upbeat Forever" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Urban Gauntlet
description: Action-y intense like percussion based piece. Need to defuse a bomb while riding in a pedi-cab? This should work well for that. Or anything where tension needs to be maintained.
credit: "Urban Gauntlet" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vadodora
description: Quite a hip little tune. Also available without the melody.
credit: "Vadodora" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vadodora Chill Mix
description: Quite a hip little tune. Also available witha cutting melody.
credit: "Vadodora Chill Mix" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Valse Gymnopedie
description: This is Gymnopedie #1 from Erik Satie (1888), but it has a beat and you can dance to it.
credit: "Valse Gymnopedie" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vanes
description: A disturbingly sweet melody on an electric piano is accompanied with a slow and steady beat. Synth sounds undulate in the background, fighting for prominence. They ultimately melt away, leaving the piano melody to play one last despair-filled refrain.
credit: "Vanes" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vanishing
description: Several distinct moods are found in this piece. They start at 0:00, 1:23, 2:31, and 3:10. They do all flow into each other, but can be sliced apart pretty easily. Some are quite beautiful, so stick with this piece. Excellent piece for filmmakers!
credit: "Vanishing" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Variation on Egmont
description: Kind of techno, with a mix in of themes from Beethoven's overture as played on piano.
credit: "Variation on Egmont" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vegas Glitz
description: This sounds happier than anything with parallel chords should.
credit: "Vegas Glitz" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Verano Sensual
description: This one was designed to be played at low volumes under people doing things like talking or fixing broken PS4s. Spicy, spicy broken PS4s. Mmmm....
credit: "Verano Sensual" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Very Low Note
description: Just a very low note (a C) to be used as a bed for any very unnerving and dark scene.
credit: "Very Low Note" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vibe Ace
description: Starts more synthy ends more organic.
credit: "Vibe Ace" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vibing Over Venus
description: It is relaxation hour here on Radio Kilimanjaro, the only all-live music, 24-hour frequency on your radio dial! Tonight is going to kick off with Alice Goodworth on her vibraphone, playing along to the famous Radio Kilimanjaro Automaton Ensemble. She calls this piece "Vibing Over Venus"... and you all know why! (It is because she plays vibes... [which is a musical instrument.])
credit: "Vibing Over Venus" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vicious
description: Bit of swing in your rap? Sure! Why not! I like swing... but NOT TOO MUCH! Just here and there... you know, to alleviate the monotony. Sort of like that one teacher you had in Social Studies that unexpectedly did something cool - like play a game - but only twice a year... and they were both in the first month, so all you ended up with was 8 months of continual disappointment. Screw you, Mr. Meuller! I still don't care about checks and balances!
credit: "Vicious" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Video Dungeon Boss
description: This a simple "fake bit" composition. I used very simple oscillators for everything, and then processed it quite a bit. Made for a dungeon level for an old-school video game. Loopable. Video Dungeon Crawl is similar but slower.
credit: "Video Dungeon Boss" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Video Dungeon Crawl
description: This a simple "fake bit" composition. I used very simple oscillators for everything, and then processed it quite a bit. Made for a dungeon level for an old-school video game. Loopable. Video Dungeon Boss is similar but faster.
credit: "Video Dungeon Crawl" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Village Consort
description: Picture a pixellated medieval village... cause that's what this is. It is the kind of music we think they played back in the day. It is not historically. But I'm okay with that, because we also didn't have lich-kings, lich-mages, lich-illithids, lich-warriors, or lich-archers. We did have lichens, though... I like lichens!
credit: "Village Consort" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Village Dawn
description: Light piece in 5/8 time with a Lydian subsection.
credit: "Village Dawn" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Villainous Treachery
description: The melody for this piece is in the bass keys, while the high notes play a headache-splitting constant rhythm. At the one-minute mark the high-pitched notes drop several octaves to play a crunched staccato before returning to the previous theme. The last thirty seconds feature drawn out chords, and the tempo slows dramatically, ending with frustrated trills in both registers, signaling the demise of the villain.
credit: "Villainous Treachery" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Villainous Treachery - Distressed
description: The melody for this piece is in the bass keys, while the high notes play a headache-splitting constant rhythm. At the one-minute mark the high-pitched notes drop several octaves to play a crunched staccato before returning to the previous theme. The last thirty seconds feature drawn out chords, and the tempo slows dramatically, ending with frustrated trills in both registers, signaling the demise of the villain.
credit: "Villainous Treachery - Distressed" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vintage Education
description: Intended to imitate the style of the 1970's educational programming.
credit: "Vintage Education" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Virtutes Instrumenti
description: Based on 11th century sacred music, this piece can set you way way back in time almost instantly. Several faster and slower sections are available during this piece.
credit: "Virtutes Instrumenti" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Virtutes Vocis
description: Based on 11th century sacred music, this pieces carries melodies only, and no words.
credit: "Virtutes Vocis" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vision of Persistence
description: Rhythmically driven simple piece, high and sweet.
credit: "Vision of Persistence" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vivacity
description: Happy, peppy, vibraphone piece. Sounds like the late 1950's or early 1960's.
credit: "Vivacity" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Voice Over Under
description: This is a piece of music classified as "GNDN". Goes Nowhere. Does Nothing. It sort of sits there and just repeats mild variants. There isn't even an ending.  Yet, this was all on purpose. This piece was designed for keeping energy in news reports or review segments where there is a lot of talking. There is no end so it is easy to loop to any length. There will come a time in your editing career where you will need this piece. Best to download it now.
credit: "Voice Over Under" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Volatile Reaction
description: 7/4 time, blasting brass, pounding percussion. Suitable for fights, evil, or a calm day at the park... in hell.
credit: "Volatile Reaction" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Voltaic
description: You know that sound that was big in 80s dance music with that sort of galloping doo-do-do-DAH-do-do-doo-do-do-DAH thing? This has a thing like that, but in really, really complex drum sound. You need to wait until 16 seconds in to hear what the doo-do-do-DAH-do-do-doo-do-do-DAH sounds like. I know it can be difficult reading KRN (Kevin's Rhythmic Notation). A-do-do-dooo-a-da-da-daaah is all I want to say to you.
credit: "Voltaic" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vortex
description: Blatting brass ensemble. Uneven phrasing.
credit: "Vortex" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Voxel Revolution
description: Is it chiptunes? Nope. Is it 80s? Nope. We had to wait 40 years for this stupid fusion! 40 Years!!! It is really happy, though. Like when an underdog video game character is doing a level-up montage, or that song that plays in a 13 year old's head when they get an extra mozzarella stick.
credit: "Voxel Revolution" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Vulcan
description: A mystical piece for Flutes, Bells, and Percussion.  Disjointed melodic flute in counterpoint with lower fluttery flutes, plodding  percussion, and shimmering bells. Same texture throughout piece.
credit: "Vulcan" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Wagner Bridal Chorus
description: The classic "here come the bride" piece written by Wagner for the opera Lohengrin. This is about as traditional a performance as you can get.
credit: "Wagner Bridal Chorus" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Wagner Bridal Chorus - piano
description: A newer piano variation on Wagner's Bridal Chorus. It leaves out some of the less familiar middle section, and changes up a few chords while retaining the melody.
credit: "Wagner Bridal Chorus - piano" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Wagon Wheel
description: Super jaunty quick tune with 3 distinct parts. The main theme starts in the beginning, Super syncopated theme starts at about a minute in, and the industrial comedy theme starts at 1:30 or so.
credit: "Wagon Wheel" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Wagon Wheel - Electronic
description: Super jaunty quick tune with 3 distinct parts. The main theme starts in the beginning, Super syncopated theme starts at about a minute in, and the industrial comedy theme starts at 1:30 or so.
credit: "Wagon Wheel - Electronic" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Wah Game Loop
description: Just a simple funk/rock piece for looping anonymously in the background of things. Organ seems a bit nasal. hmm...
credit: "Wah Game Loop" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Walking Along
description: Written as a laid-back background for a film where a calming feel was needed.
credit: "Walking Along" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Wallpaper
description: Very very clean mix that is non-offensive on almost all fronts. Good spectral distribution - nice lows and highs. 2 catchy synth lines sort of fight for attention, leaving you to ignore them both after a while.
credit: "Wallpaper" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Waltz of the Carnies
description: Creepy off-putting circus music. Also features some honking horns later in the piece.
credit: "Waltz of the Carnies" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Waltz of Treachery
description: Light but dim. Nice for a 'classy' villain with a plan.
credit: "Waltz of Treachery" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Waltz Primordial
description: Featuring the genuine Nordic Metal talents of Alexander Nakarada.
credit: "Waltz Primordial" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Waltz (Tschikovsky Op. 40)
description: Opus 40; Number 9. Written 1878. Recorded 2005.
credit: "Waltz (Tschikovsky Op. 40)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Water Droplets on the River
description: 6/8 piece meant to be reminiscent of nice memories from long ago.
credit: "Water Droplets on the River" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Water Lily
description: Simple and elegant.
credit: "Water Lily" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Water Prelude
description: Smooth background music... Float-y feeling.
credit: "Water Prelude" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Waunobe March
description: A simple march as played by a semi-competent 23-piece ensemble.
credit: "Waunobe March" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: We Got Trouble
description: Super action, but still a bit restrained. Quite a long cue with a few changes on the inside.
credit: "We Got Trouble" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: We Wish you a Merry Christmas
description: Starts out slowly and accelerates as it builds.
credit: "We Wish you a Merry Christmas" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Weight of Responsibility
description: Brass ensemble with a slight bit of strings. Deliberate chorale sounding, free conducted. Evocative of a sense of nobility and weariness. Loopable.
credit: "Weight of Responsibility" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Welcome to HorrorLand
description: Welcome to HorrorLand! Please keep all arms, legs, and eyestalks inside the vehicle at all times. All exits are clearly marked. There are no exits. Do not attempt to leave HorrorLand. This will end badly for everyone. Please note: it will end badly if you do not attempt to leave as well. So, it is really up to you. Feel free to split up your group and explore. That is always a great idea!
credit: "Welcome to HorrorLand" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Welcome to the Show
description: A one-chord wonder designed to open a show. It has a long lead out for fading. Modulation about halfway through.
credit: "Welcome to the Show" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Wepa
description: Need an upbeat vaguely urban-sounding piece to run under your video outro? That's why I made this! You're welcome.
credit: "Wepa" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Werq
description: This is destined to be a podcast theme. If you're starting a podcast, get this now before someone else does. You know it's perfect. Plus is is easy to type the title in your credits. I'm looking out for you, podcaster! All hail the Podfather, Adam Curry. Yes, that Adam Curry. Yes, he really did invent podcasts.
credit: "Werq" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Western Streets
description: An all percussion tension-sustaining piece... More chaotic than symmetric, but enough repeated themes to keep it cohesive.
credit: "Western Streets" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Wet Riffs
description: Solo bass with a looping pedal. Very very slow. Super nice. Starts with the highs, and builds interest in the bass.
credit: "Wet Riffs" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: What Child is This
description: Very very high and thin.
credit: "What Child is This" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: What Is Love
description: What is love? Apparently, it is an odd mix of 1980's synthy love songs and modern trap beats. I don't think there is anything like this out there... which may be a fine thing - or I've just invented a genre. Crooner-Synth Trap-Pop.
credit: "What Is Love" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: What You Want
description: Super aggressive distorted piece with vocal effects.
credit: "What You Want" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: What You Want (version 2)
description: Same as the other version, but with no intelligible vocals.
credit: "What You Want (version 2)" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: When The Wind Blows
description: Several wind instruments play lilting melodies that are slow and meander through the piece, sometimes bordering on being slightly out of tune. The calm music has an edge of solemnity about it. The ever-present acoustic guitar is methodical and resembles a pulse ? it exists but is forgotten, except when the guitar draws out the length of a note.
credit: "When The Wind Blows" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Whimsy Groove
description: Lighter and more fun small drum ensemble. Tumba, Conga, Quinto, Bells, and lots of Marimba.
credit: "Whimsy Groove" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Whiskey on the Mississippi
description: With a jumping bass and off-beat syncopation, this is straight from Memphis? Beale Street. The Hammond organ and electric guitar play together as longtime friends, while the melody changes hands from guitar to organ to electric piano.
credit: "Whiskey on the Mississippi" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: White
description: Easy flowing with highly differentiated right and left hand parts.
credit: "White" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: White Lotus
description: Interesting new age sort of piece, that meets you halfway in the beginning with a lush, but brittle metallic soundscape. As it progresses - the metals fall away, and you're left with a bed of pure sine waves, and a piano tuned exactly to go along with them.
credit: "White Lotus" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Who Likes to Party
description: There are 70s bits, 80s bits, 90s bits.... all soft of mashed up in a salad-mash-soup-like thing.  Super crisp dance mix.
credit: "Who Likes to Party" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Wholesome
description: Nothing but good, wholesome instruments here. None of those dirty electric guitars, synths, drum kits, harps, sackbuts, or pipe organs. Heh, organs.

title: Windswept
description: A relaxed guitar and strings piece for the denouement of a story or exposition of the scenic outdoors. The guitar is peaceful as the strings gently build in prominence. The tempo is regular overall, but slows down in key moments to build a sense of tranquility.
credit: "Windswept" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Winner Winner!

title: Winter Chimes

title: With a Creation
description: An experimental piece, designed to emulate a keyboardist with her robot.  The piano player likes to play with the EP in this piece.  Take a listen to get the full effect.  EP used heavily throughout the entire piece.  Build at 1:02, percussion picks up with heavy, fast beats.

title: Wretched Destroyer
description: Have you ever heard a 4 bassoon ensemble before? Not likely. While bassoonists may create temporary pair-bonds, they are never found in groups of 3 or more. Much digital trickery was involved in this piece to make them appear as though they were all in the same room at the same time. Tuba players, on the other hand exhibit extreme flocking behaviour, and have even been spotted in mass migrations.
credit: "Wretched Destroyer" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Yallahs

credit: "Yallahs" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Your Call

credit: "Your Call" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Zanzibar
description: Energetic without being aggressive. This one has a nice flow and interesting changes.

title: Zap Beat

title: Zazie
description: Hey there, swingers and swingees! Grab your berets and cigarettes for this trip to a hip Euro-Space-Age Lounge Music Adventure! Vous ne devriez pas amener un canard à combattre les Belges. Il est important d'avoir un mot de passe fort. Vous souvenez-vous de "Le Manège enchanté"? Parce que je ne me souviens pas de ça.
credit: "Zazie" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: ZigZag
description: A little aggressive, a little chill, a little groovy, a little cool. Not entirely appropriate for all occasions, but in the right context - it may be just what you need! This is the "Goth 7th-Grader" of the music world. The instrument with the sharp chord hits is the mighty Mellotron, which is a pre-sampler sort of analog keyboard attached to a bunch of tape players. I cheated. This one is digital.
credit: "ZigZag" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Zombie Chase
description: Aggressive, but smooth action sequence; earthy and powerful, using the same piano theme as Zombie Hoodoo.
credit: "Zombie Chase" Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com). Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 License, http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

title: Zombie Hoodoo
description: Simple piano line with dark atmospherics in the background. It says "Zombie", but it is useful for any number of creepy motifs. (This piece is related to Zombie Chase).
